title: Teamlead EHS Manager  Southern Germany, Austria & Switzerland (m/w/d)
jd_text: Job Description Summary The Project EHS Manager HVDC (m/f/d) is GE Vernova’s lead Environment, Health & Safety representative on during the planning and execution on a German HVDC project team and the main HVDC contact to our customer. The role is responsible for development and driving all EHS aspects within the project scope, ensuring full compliance with applicable legal, customer, and GE Vernova requirements, and promoting a strong safety culture across the whole project, including integration of EHS aspects with our partners at the shipyards and offshore. The Project EHS Manager works in close partnership with the project leadership, the site EHS managers and the EHS roles of our consortium partners and subcontractors to prevent injuries, control risks, protect the environment, promote the health for everyone involved in the project and ensure disciplined implementation of project EHS plans, procedures, and standards. Job Description Key Responsibilities EHS Leadership & General EHS Management Act as the primary EHS leader and focal point for the entire project including the EHS interface to the customer. Provide visible EHS leadership and proactive support to the Project Management, consortium partners and subcontractors Build and promote a strong safety culture and ensure EHS is embedded across all project activities Support the implementation of GE Vernova EHS strategy, standards and programs, Serve as the key EHS interface for customer, consortium partner and subcontractors Understand regulatory changes and trends and forecast business impacts. Perform and coordinate the delivery of EHS trainings, ensuring the competency of personnel within their scope. Support project management to implement, monitor and continuously improve the project’s EHS management and performance in line with GE Vernova requirements and applicable standards Conduct and facilitate risk assessments and hazard analyses; define, track and verify corrective and preventive actions Plan and perform EHS audits, inspections and site walks; follow up on findings and support closure in a timely manner Support the application of “Design for EHS” in projects (e.g. engineering controls, safe work methods, layout and access concepts) Promote Safety as the first priority for all actors in the project - communicating pro-actively and leading by exemplary behavior Report to EHS Functional Leader as well as project organization (dotted line) EHS Reporting, Incident Management & Learning Conduct EHS reporting in line with GE Vernova processes and timelines (KPIs, dashboards, monthly/quarterly reports) Ensure accurate and timely registration, classification and escalation of incidents, near misses and unsafe conditions in the designated EHS tools Coordinate together with the regional EHS leader and the project management team the incident investigation and reports, ensure that investigations of accidents and compliance incidents are conducted, documented, and reported as required. Track action implementation and effectiveness; share lessons learned and best practices across projects, sites and teams Safety Culture, Training, and Workforce Engagement Lead and support project EHS meetings and campaign activities Coordinate and reinforce GE Vernova safety culture programs across the project Ensure EHS expectations are clearly communicated to employees, contractors, and visitors Promote workforce engagement and encourage active participation in hazard reporting, observations, and continuous improvement Subcontractor EHS Management Verify EHS competency, qualifications, and readiness of subcontractors mobilized to site Monitor subcontractor compliance with approved EHS plans, legal requirements, and project rules Support onboarding, performance reviews, and interventions where subcontractor EHS performance is below expectations Qualifications / Requirements Education & Professional Experience Bachelor’s degree in Safety Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Engineering, Occupational Health & Safety or related field or technical/vocational qualification with substantial relevant professional EHS experience Recognized qualification as Fachkraft für Arbeitssicherheit (Safety Specialist) according to German regulations (DGUV) as well as SiGEKo Proven experience in lead EHS role, ideally in construction, installation or industrial project environments in HV electrical environments Solid knowledge of German occupational health & safety and environmental regulations as well as environmental management on construction sites and permit-to-work and control-of-work systems Experience in multi-national projects and work environments Language & IT Skills Fluent German (spoken and written) Good English (spoken and written), including the ability to prepare documentation, reporting and trainings in both languages Confident user of MS Office; title: Sr Director Analyst - AI Technology Economics
jd_text: This is an individual contributor role About the role: Gartner is building the industry's leading Tech Market Economics capability to understand where AI creates, captures and destroys value across the technology ecosystem, from trillion-dollar infrastructure investments to the economics of technology providers. As a Senior Director Analyst, you will lead the development of a new generation of data-driven Gartner positions, partnering with our Tech Market Economics Modelling, Data Science and Data Engineering teams to uncover insights others cannot and scale their impact across Gartner's global research footprint. The role demands exceptional judgment and intellectual curiosity. You will draw on emerging signals, novel data sources and pioneering analytical approaches, combining your expertise with the broader models, data assets and methodologies of Tech Market Economics. Success comes from recognizing when disparate signals converge to an insight worthy of Gartner's voice. The most valuable insights rarely emerge from a single dataset, model or methodology. They emerge from synthesizing multiple forms of evidence into judgements that initially appear impossible to make, but become irrefutable once the underlying economics, signals and market dynamics are understood. title: Advanced Lead Engineer - Commercial Field Service
jd_text: Job Description Summary As an Advanced Lead Engineer – Commercial Field Service, you will get the unique opportunity to serve as the primary on-site representative for our customer and a single point of contact for key internal stakeholders before, during, and after aircraft entry into service. Job Description Key Roles & Responsibilities: Our FSEs embody our mission, embedded within the customers site, delivering exceptional service and support. Operating autonomously and remotely from GE Aerospace hubs to resolve technical challenges and drive success, directly in support of our customers’ fleets. More specifically, you will: Provide Leadership and Technical Support: Offer technical direction and assistance to the customers operation, inspections, maintenance, and repair of assigned fleets.​ Customer Advocacy: Deliver prompt, effective solutions that address customer issues and exceed their expectations, driving loyalty and long-term partnerships. Monitor and Improve Reliability: Track reliability and on-wing performance, including significant events, engine removals, delays, and cancellations. Influence airline stakeholders to implement critical reliability improvements. Enhance Maintenance Planning: Influence maintenance planning to ensure the stability of the aircraft engine fleet.​ Evaluate Maintenance Effectiveness: Review the effectiveness of maintenance actions to identify opportunities for improvement.​ Apply FLIGHT DECK: Utilize our FLIGHT DECK principles to deliver continuous improvement, identifying proactive reliability enhancements. Data Analytics and Reporting: Produce data analytics and timely reports on fleet status, program updates, events, and trends for key internal stakeholders.​ Proactive Maintenance Recommendations: Provide recommendations for proactive maintenance based on engine performance analytics.​ Required Qualifications: To be considered for this opportunity, candidates must have: A Bachelor of Engineering or technical degree from an accredited university or college (or a high school diploma / GED / technical certificate with at least 6 years of full-time work experience in airline operations or maintenance planning, engineering, aviation propulsion, or other related field). A minimum of 4 years of full-time working experience in airline operations or maintenance planning, engineering, aviation propulsion, or other related field Desired Characteristics: Technical expertise in aircraft engine or turbomachinery equipment Experience using software or data analytics to make informed technical decisions and to provide recommendations to the customer or other key internal stakeholders Self-directed with the ability to problem solve using sound judgement and critical thinking Ability to lead and deliver on result orientated priorities using strong project management, analytical, time management and prioritization skills Strong oral and written communication skills with the ability to forge deep relations at all levels, not only with key internal stakeholders but also with the customer Passion to gain a deeper understanding of the commercial function and driving success for Aerospace with internal/external stakeholders, our customers, partners and colleagues Embody the GE Leadership Behaviors: Respect for People: As an FSE, you’ll foster a collaborative environment with our customers, building strong relationships and trust. You’ll be the technical on-site representative for GE Aerospace. Continuous Improvement: We’re committed to excellence and constantly seek ways to enhance and improve technical performance. Customer Driven: Understanding, prioritizing, and communicating the needs of our customers is at the heart of our field service team. Delivering prompt, effective solutions that exceed customer expectations, driving long-term partnerships.​ Additional Information Relocation: This position is eligible for international/domestic relocation support. Travel: Candidates should anticipate up to 25% travel per year in this role. title: Executive Partner, Chief Product Officers - High Tech
jd_text: Executive Partner (EP) – Tech Chief Product Officer About the Role: The Executive Partner (EP) is a senior advisor to Chief Product Officers (CPOs) at leading global high-tech organizations. As an EP, your primary responsibility is to deliver value that directly results in client retention by connecting clients with Gartner’s world-class research, analyst expertise, and broader community. You will help clients identify and achieve their most critical priorities by leveraging Gartner’s resources, insights, and network—ensuring Gartner is seen as indispensable to their success. What You Will Do: Manage a portfolio of C-level client relationships, acting as a trusted advisor and primary point of contact for CPOs. Drive client retention by proactively connecting clients with the most relevant Gartner research, analysts, and peer communities to address their mission-critical priorities. Define and deliver innovative, tailored service solutions by assessing each client’s business context, priorities, and goals, and developing a customized value plan. Lead and participate in Gartner Executive Series webinars, peer networking sessions, and community-building activities for CPOs. Build a strong local and virtual community of CPOs, fostering open dialogue and knowledge sharing. Collaborate closely with internal Gartner teams—including Sales, Research, and Client Service—to ensure seamless service delivery, high engagement, and successful renewals. Support research activities by facilitating client participation in studies and panels, and by providing client feedback to Gartner’s research organization. Contribute to account planning and value demonstration activities in partnership with Sales to drive both retention and growth. What Success Looks Like: High client retention rates driven by clear, measurable value delivered through Gartner research, analyst connections, and community engagement. Clients consistently view Gartner as a critical partner in achieving their business outcomes. Strong, collaborative relationships with Sales and Research teams, resulting in successful renewals and new business growth. What You Will Need: 10+ years’ experience in a senior product leadership role (VP/SVP/Head of Product) with a track record of managing significant product portfolios and leading product teams, or engagement manager experience in management consulting supporting CPOs / Heads of Product. Deep expertise in the Enterprise Application Software, Infrastructure Software or Security markets, with an understanding of the unique challenges and opportunities in the space. title: Americas Consulting Director
jd_text: Job Description Summary The Consulting Director – Americas leads the regional Functional Consulting team and is accountable for translating implementation expertise into sustained customer outcomes. The role manages and develops the team, ensures disciplined resource and delivery execution, and partners closely with Customer Success Managers and the broader Customer Success organization to accelerate adoption, improve time to value, mitigate retention risk, and identify expansion opportunities. This leader establishes a consistent customer-adoption operating model across the Americas, coordinates effectively with global adoption, product, project management, technical consulting, support, sales, and quality teams, and maintains clear visibility to priorities, capacity, risks, outcomes, and follow-through. High levels of leadership judgment, customer focus, operational rigor, and cross-functional influence are required. Job Description Roles and Responsibilities Lead, coach, and develop the Americas Functional Consulting team, including senior professionals and people leaders; set clear priorities, build capability, manage performance and succession, promote inclusion, and attract and retain strong talent. Own regional execution of the customer-adoption program in partnership with Customer Success Managers. Prioritize accounts using customer outcomes, adoption health, annual recurring revenue, retention risk, contractual commitments, and growth potential. Establish and maintain one coordinated adoption plan per customer, beginning during implementation where appropriate and covering stabilization, core adoption, expansion, optimization, and sustained value realization. Ensure plans identify outcomes, milestones, owners, risks, dependencies, and measures of success. Align the consulting team with the regional and global Customer Success organization so adoption definitions, health measures, account priorities, engagement models, and customer communications are consistent. Clarify ownership and handoffs among Customer Success Managers, global adoption, project management, technical consulting, support, product, sales, and quality teams. Act as a trusted partner to Customer Success leadership and account teams by providing timely visibility to customer health, adoption progress, value realization, escalations, resource constraints, and recommended interventions. Manage team capacity and deployment across implementation, adoption, acceleration-plan, non-billable intervention, training, pre-sales, and escalation support. Maintain an accurate resource forecast, make explicit prioritization decisions, and ensure effort is aligned to the highest-value customer outcomes. Drive disciplined delivery and measurable impact, including implementation readiness, adoption milestones, time to value, utilization, customer satisfaction, quality, margin, retention support, and expansion enablement. Establish clear operating rhythms and follow through on commitments. Use industry experience, equipment knowledge, software expertise, and consultative skills to guide solution design and enablement for predictive analytics, asset performance management, and other digital offerings. Build repeatable methods, templates, playbooks, and knowledge-sharing practices that improve implementation consistency and adoption outcomes across the team. Promote practical use of automation and AI within approved governance. Use Lean as the team’s operating system to focus on customer value, standard work, daily management, root-cause problem solving, and continuous improvement. Integrate applicable quality frameworks and customer-focused KPIs into team execution. Use voice-of-customer, employee-engagement, and delivery feedback to improve team effectiveness and customer experience. Create an environment in which team members raise risks early, learn from mistakes, and act on feedback. Interpret internal and external business challenges, industry trends, and customer needs to recommend improvements to products, services, processes, and go-to-market execution. Represent the Americas consulting perspective in cross-functional decisions. Lead complex cross-functional initiatives and customer escalations with moderate-to-high risk or ambiguity. Communicate clearly with leaders and customers, challenge conflicting or incomplete information, negotiate priorities, and mobilize the right resources to achieve outcomes. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, business, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience. At least 15 years of progressively responsible experience in industrial software, asset performance management, asset integrity, reliability, plant maintenance, engineering consulting, or a closely related field, including significant experience in customer-facing services and complex enterprise implementations. Minimum of 5 years of people leadership experience, with a proven track record of leading experienced consulting professionals and/or people leaders across geographically dispersed teams. Demonstrated success driving team performance, developing talent, optimizing resource deployment, and delivering exceptional customer outcomes in complex, customer-facing environments. Proven record of advising senior customer stakeholders, leading high-complexity engagements and escalations, and translating technical and operational expertise into adoption, value realization, retention, and growth. Desired Characteristics Deep domain expertise in one or more relevant industrial sectors, with a strong understanding of asset integrity, risk-based inspection, reliability, plant maintenance, predictive analytics, data quality, and asset performance management. Broad experience advising multiple enterprise customers across countries, operating environments, and regulatory contexts; able to adapt proven practices without losing consistency or rigor. Recognized technical and consultative credibility with customer executives, engineering and maintenance leaders, practitioners, and internal product teams; able to challenge assumptions and guide consequential decisions. Demonstrated success moving customers beyond implementation to sustained adoption and measurable value realization, including the ability to diagnose data, process, capability, and change-management barriers. Experience establishing operating mechanisms across Consulting, Customer Success, Product, Sales, Support, and Quality, with transparent measures, clear decision rights, and effective escalation paths. Evidence of external professional leadership—such as participation in industry standards bodies, technical committees, conferences, publications, or professional communities—is highly valued. Strong oral and written communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex technical and business issues clearly to executives and customers. Strong interpersonal and leadership skills, with a record of coaching senior talent, building followership, and creating accountability in a matrixed organization. Demonstrated ability to analyze ambiguous problems, make sound trade-offs, and resolve issues at their root cause. Demonstrated ability to lead complex programs and execute with discipline across organizational boundaries. title: Software Engineering Manager - Order Fulfillment Software Factory
location: Austin, Texas, United States of America
jd_text: Job Description The Role The Order Fulfillment Software Factory delivers GM’s end-to-end software for two value streams. Source to Deliver covers purchasing, supplier management, supply chain, and logistics. Order to Deliver covers how GM sells, configures, schedules, and delivers vehicles to dealers and customers. The factory is advancing GM’s SaaS First, Cloud First, and AI First direction. It works closely with GPSC Business Area IT, Sales and Marketing Business IT, and GM’s peer software engineering, mainframe, and SAP factories to deliver consistent, modern solutions at speed. We’re looking for a Software Engineering Manager who codes. You’ll lead a team of approximately 6–12 engineers with a mix of skills, sometimes including a technical lead or first-line lead, that owns a product or service area such as Vehicle Order Management, Order Scheduling, or Global Logistics. You’ll be the team’s technical anchor: scoping complex problems, designing systems, and shipping alongside your engineers. You’ll also make agentic AI coding the default way your team builds, tests, and operates software. This is a player-coach role. We expect you to spend approximately 30–40% of your time hands-on, including writing and reviewing production code, designing systems, prototyping, and working daily with AI coding agents. You’ll set your team’s technical direction and be accountable for its delivery, quality, and growth. What You’ll Do Lead the Team’s Delivery and Direction Turn the factory’s strategy into clear direction, objectives, and operating plans for your team. Allocate resources, delegate work, and reprioritize as business needs change. Own your team’s metrics and KPIs, including delivery, quality, reliability, and business outcomes, and make measurable contributions to the factory’s goals. Drive strategy and implementation for large projects that affect multiple departments and business partners, including GPSC, dealers, and suppliers. Tie technical initiatives to key business objectives and begin building your area’s technology roadmap with Product Management. Handle competing demands, sensitive situations, and conflicts within the team and with other teams. Build alignment with stakeholders who are skeptical of new approaches. Be accountable for workforce planning and operational and financial decisions in your area, including cloud and AI tooling spend. Lead Hands-On Act as the technical lead for your team’s workstream. Write, review, and merge production code for critical-path features, complex defects, and proofs of concept. Design software systems and define architecture for team-level projects, including services, APIs, event-driven integrations, data models, and SaaS/ERP integrations. Participate in architecture reviews across the factory. Guide engineers as they scope complex problems and develop creative, pragmatic solutions. Be the team’s go-to resource for technology, cross-team interfaces, and company policies and processes. Propose new technology that changes how the business works, with forward-looking impact on product experience, quality, and time to market. Own operational excellence. Participate in on-call, lead incident response and postmortems, and deliver high-quality work on schedule, with quality as the priority. Make Your Team Agent-Native Make AI coding agents, such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot agent mode, and Cursor, part of everyday work across planning, implementation, testing, code review, refactoring and migrations, documentation, and operations. Build and maintain the team’s agent setup, including repository-level agent instruction and context files, reusable prompts and skills, MCP and other tool integrations with internal systems, and CI pipelines that run agents for automated pull-request review, test generation, and dependency upgrades. Set guardrails so agent-generated code is safe to ship, including test coverage and evaluation checks, human-review standards, sandboxing and permissions, secret and data handling, and provenance checks. Use agents to modernize legacy order and supply chain systems faster, for example by generating test harnesses for legacy code, running automated migrations, and documenting undocumented systems. Track impact through measures such as cycle time, change-failure rate, defect escape rate, and developer experience. Share what works with peer teams and help establish factory-wide practices. Build and Grow the Team Hire engineers and make internal and external staffing decisions to build the right mix of talent and experience. Hold regular one-on-ones and career conversations. Plan people resources so engineers continue to grow, and assign work that plays to each person’s strengths. Run performance management, including goal setting, feedback, calibration, and addressing underperformance. Apply company policies consistently and fairly. Coach engineers to direct, verify, and own AI-generated work, and to maintain a high bar for everything they merge. Champion change management as the team adopts agentic development. Role-model GM’s Behaviors while making room for individuality and diverse perspectives. Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications) Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Applied Science in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Mathematics, Information Technology, Information Security, Cybersecurity, or a related field plus 6–9 years of relevant experience; or 10–12 years of full-time relevant experience. At least 2 years of experience managing a team of software engineers with varied skill levels, including hiring, coaching, and performance management. title: Inventory Specialist - San Antonio
jd_text: JOB OVERVIEW: The Inventory Specialist is responsible for managing all aspects of the integrity of Henry Schein’s dental inventory within assigned 3PL locations and local centers; responsible to complete all inventory audits, identifies inventory deficiencies, develops the solution and implements strategic plans to ensure compliance with Company inventory standards. The position is accountable for between $2-4 million of inventory across multiple 3PL locations and centers across their assigned territory. Plays a critical role in supporting operational success in assigned centers of operation. Responsible for supporting and reporting on various aspects of Henry Schein’s operational policies and procedures. This can include but is not limited to coordinating with different departments, optimizing operational workflow, ensuring inventory compliance, presenting to leadership and Finance, and reconciling operational errors. This position will play an active role in cost savings initiatives, will lead through influence to reduce inventory write-offs, and be held accountable to results. Please note : This is a fully on-site, Monday - Friday position based out of our San Antonio, TX location. The position follows standard business hours, and candidates must be located within a reasonable commuting distance of the location. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Receives all inventory and maintains accurate records of shipments and goods received for all assigned centers of operation. Works in conjunction with internal Equipment Coordination Specialist (ECS) team to manage and reconcile all inventory shipped to customers and other locations to ensure the right equipment is delivered on time, as per customer invoicing. Conducts physical inventory audits and spot audits for all assigned centers of operation, researches any deficiencies and identifies solutions. Oversees inventory in assigned centers of operation by ensuring all 3PL and center cycle count requirements, inventory management and audits are completed successfully and timely. Manage all consignments, equipment rental returns, and warranty returns (RMA) processes for assigned centers of operation. Travel to locations in assigned areas to uncover operational inefficiencies in both Henry Schein and 3PL facilities. Report findings to leadership with suggested action plan to eliminate errors and inefficiencies. Reconcile all inventory audits to maintain acceptable inventory levels in the 3PLs and centers. Reduce operational costs by reconciling missing, lost, and wrongfully transacted inventory. Develops and maintains exceptional working relationships with vendors (3PL’s), ECS and local management team. Collaborate with team members and cross functional departments to resolve operational issues and optimize workflow. Reduce depreciated, obsolete inventory by working with Area leadership to develop ways to liquidate to save on operational costs. Oversee assigned center’s systematic locations to ensure inventory is accurately represented and accounted for. Report on assigned centers of operation key performance indicators to identify historical and trending data relating to operational performance. SPECIFIC KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS: Advanced in Microsoft Software (Excel, Word, PowerPoint). Experience working across various data entry platforms. Strong logistics experience with high volume inventory movement. Interpersonal skills to work efficiently with others (Vendors, TSM’s, 3PL’s) for detailed follow-up. GENERAL SKILLS & COMPETENCIES: Strong time management skills and the ability to prioritize work Very good attention to detail and accuracy Customer service oriented and ability to work with and resolve complex issues Ability to plan and arrange activities Excellent interpersonal communication skills Excellent written and verbal communication skills Ability to maintain confidential and highly sensitive information Ability to work in a team environment Ability to multi-task Ability to manage conflict Capacity to work effectively under pressure Analytical thinking Oversee small projects Identify and recommend continuous improvement opportunities Establish productive working relationships at multiple levels within the organization MINIMUM WORK EXPERIENCE: 4 years combined experience in equipment installation, purchasing and customer service, order processing, sales operations, inventory management or the equivalent required. PREFERRED EDUCATION: Typically High School education, vocational training and/or on-the-job training. Bachelor’s degree preferred. TRAVEL / PHYSICAL DEMANDS: Some local travel between assigned locations (up to 25%-30%) may be required to perform monthly and quarterly cycle counts at assigned distribution centers and third-party logistics locations. The amount of travel may vary based on business needs and number of assigned locations. This position currently supports two locations in the San Antonio, TX area. title: Senior Transformation Analyst, Data & Value
jd_text: Forming Our Future together FormFactor, Inc. (NASDAQ: FORM), is a leading provider of essential test and measurement technologies along the full semiconductor product life cycle — from characterization, modeling, reliability, and design de-bug, to qualification and production test. Semiconductor companies rely upon FormFactor’s products and services to accelerate profitability by optimizing device performance and advancing yield knowledge. The company serves customers through its network of facilities in Asia, Europe, and North America. Rooted in our core values — Focus on the Customer, Ownership & Accountability, Respectfully & Effectively Communicate, and Motivate & Develop People — we foster an environment where diverse perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated. Everyone can make an impact here. Whether it's improving products, supporting customers, or positively influencing peers and the community, the contributions of our people matter. Shift: The regular hours for this position are day shift. Job Description: FormFactor is seeking a highly skilled and motivated Senior Transformation Analyst to provide the analytical and technical foundation for the company’s highest-priority cross-functional transformation initiatives. This role will combine strong technical expertise with business and financial acumen to develop business cases, financial and operational models, portfolio dashboards, executive decision packages, and benefit-validation reporting. The successful candidate will be a hands-on individual contributor who can move from an ambiguous business problem to a trusted fact base, analytical model, executive recommendation, and sustainable reporting solution. This individual will work closely with Finance leadership, business units, IT, data engineering, and cross-functional teams and will have experience with data modeling, visualization, automation, Power BI, Tableau, Oracle Analytics Cloud, Qlik or similar tools, Python, SQL, and related analytics approaches. Key Responsibilities: Transformation Analytics and Business Cases Translate complex business issues into clear analytical questions, hypotheses, data requirements, and decision criteria. Own business cases for transformation initiatives, including baseline performance, investment requirements, expected benefits, risks, dependencies, sensitivities, and value-realization timing. Build financial and operational models to evaluate revenue, margin, cost, cash, inventory, capacity, productivity, service, and other key drivers. Perform diagnostic, scenario, sensitivity, and driver-based analysis to quantify tradeoffs and support management decisions. Partner with Finance and functional leaders to validate assumptions, reconcile initiative economics, and refresh business cases as conditions change. Data Modeling, Analytics, and Automation Extract, combine, cleanse, transform, and analyze data from financial, commercial, planning, manufacturing, operational, and other enterprise systems. Use SQL, Python, scripting, advanced spreadsheet techniques, and similar tools to automate data preparation, perform analysis, and build repeatable models. Develop trusted data models that support consistent financial and operational analysis, forecasting, and performance management. Identify opportunities to apply predictive, diagnostic, optimization, AI, or automation approaches to transformation priorities. Partner with IT and data engineering teams to define requirements for development activities and improve data access, infrastructure, data quality, integration, governance, and reporting automation. Portfolio Dashboards and Executive Decision Support Design and maintain tools, dashboards, workflows, etc., for business partners as well as for the transformation team covering scope, milestones, decisions, risks, dependencies, resources, adoption, and value realization. Standardize metrics, hierarchies, master-data definitions, and calculation logic across transformation initiatives. Use Power BI, Tableau, Oracle Analytics Cloud, Qlik, or similar tools to create intuitive, decision-oriented visualizations for executive audiences. Own the analytical content of executive decision packages, including options, quantified impacts, risks, recommendations, decision owners, and required timing. Maintain decision logs and supporting datasets to create traceability from management decision through implementation and outcome. Apply appropriate development methodologies to test and release items to production. Benefit Validation and Business Partnership Define benefit baselines, KPIs, calculation methods, data sources, owners, and validation cadence at the start of each initiative. Track forecast, implemented, realized, and Finance-validated value and investigate variances between expected and actual outcomes. Ensure reported benefits are supportable, transparent, and not double-counted. Work alongside business owners to embed new metrics, models, dashboards, and decision routines into recurring management processes. Document data definitions, assumptions, procedures, and controls and transfer sustainable analytical ownership to the appropriate function. Key Deliverables: Transformation business cases and scenario models Financial and operational models supporting enterprise tradeoff decisions Executive decision packages and concise ELT reporting Portfolio dashboards, milestone views, risk registers, and decision logs Benefit baselines, validation models, and value-realization reporting Documented data definitions, analytical procedures, and sustainable handoff Preferred Qualifications & Experiences: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business Analytics, Economics, Industrial Engineering, Operations Research, Data Analytics, Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related quantitative discipline. 5+ years of experience in financial analytics, business analytics, transformation, FP&A, operations, consulting, business intelligence, or a related role. Demonstrated experience developing business cases and complex financial or operational models. Advanced Excel and hands-on experience with Power BI, Tableau, Oracle Analytics Cloud, Qlik, or a similar visualization platform. Practical SQL capability and experience using Python, scripting, low-code automation, or similar tools for data preparation, modeling, analysis, or workflow automation. Ability to reconcile large or inconsistent datasets and explain analytical methods, assumptions, and conclusions to technical and nontechnical stakeholders. Strong executive communication, organization, ownership, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Experience with ERP, EPM, CRM, planning, manufacturing, data warehouse, or enterprise performance-management systems. Experience building capacity, demand, supply, pricing, cost, gross-margin, working-capital, or productivity models. Experience with APIs, Power Query, Power Automate, notebooks, Git, forecasting, statistical analysis, optimization, machine learning, or generative AI applications. Semiconductor, semiconductor equipment, electronics, capital equipment, high-mix manufacturing, supply chain, or operations experience. Advanced degree or relevant professional certification. What Success Looks Like: Success means leaders have a trusted, concise, technically sound, and financially grounded view of transformation priorities, decisions, progress, risks, adoption, and value. Analysis improves decision speed and quality, dashboards drive accountability, benefits are transparently validated, and analytical capabilities are transferred into sustainable business ownership. Skills: Analytical Method, Application Programming Interface (API), Business Analytics, Business Intelligence (BI), Customer Relationship Management (CRM), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), Financial Analytics, Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A), Microsoft Excel, Organizational Capacity Building, Preparation of Business Cases, Statistical Analysis, Structured Query Language (SQL), Tableau (Software) Education & Experience: Minimum of 5 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 3 years and a Master’s degree; or a PhD without experience; or equivalent work | Required Equal Employment Opportunity Statement FormFactor is an equal opportunity employer. title: Workforce Scheduling Program Manager
jd_text: You’re more valuable than ever – And that’s just how we’ll make you feel. Job Summary The Workforce Scheduling Program Manager leads workforce planning, staffing, and scheduling initiatives across the organization. This role partners with Operations, Finance, Data Services, IT, and People teams to improve volume forecasting accuracy, optimize staffing strategies, and drive consistent scheduling practices that support operational performance and growth. As the business owner of workforce management processes and systems, the Program Manager uses data-driven insights to identify opportunities, implement best practices, and ensure effective workforce planning across the Company, a multi-site healthcare organization. This position plays a critical role in enhancing efficiency, standardization, and team member experience. Qualifications Education Required: Bachelor’s degree; experience will be considered in lieu of a degree. Licenses/Certifications Required: None Work Experience Required: 3+ years of workforce management or scheduling experience (e.g., forecasting, staffing models, capacity planning) in multi-site environment. 5+ years of health care experience. Scheduling experience in a medical environment. Experience in development, management, and enforcement of multi-site scheduling and payroll processes and best practices. Experience in use of scheduling systems or other standard tools to report on and analyze staffing level compliance, time punch compliance, and overtime utilization. Preferred Qualifications, Education, Licenses, Certifications, Experience, etc.: None Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities This role involves interaction and collaboration with other departments, Joint Venture team members, and health system partners and requires excellent judgment and interpersonal skills. Workforce management and staffing‑to‑model expertise across multi‑site healthcare operations. Proficiency with scheduling and time‑tracking systems and their enterprise‑wide optimization. Knowledge of timekeeping processes, clock‑in/clock‑out compliance, and overtime controls. Ability to analyze data, build reports, and monitor schedule and staffing compliance. Skill in developing and improving standard processes and best practices for scheduling and time tracking. Familiar with integrations including flat-file exports/imports and APIs between scheduling systems and other systems such as a data warehouse of HRIS. Ability to and interest in expanding technical knowledge particularly in areas of AI-driven forecasting, automated modeling, and information distribution via automated integrations. Ability to translate business requirements from operations leaders into clear technical specifications for forecasting, optimization, and reporting enhancements, and to prioritize a backlog of improvements Experience operationalizing analytics, including building or overseeing dashboards in tools such as Tableau, Power BI, Sigma, etc. to monitor model adherence, volumes, and key SLAs Strong collaboration and stakeholder‑management skills across operations, FP&A, IT, Talent Acquisition, and health‑system partners. Effective problem‑solving and sound judgment in addressing workforce and scheduling issues. Clear written and verbal communication skills for templates, guidance, and performance updates. Ability to work independently, set priorities, and meet enterprise deadlines in a remote environment. Customer‑service orientation in supporting internal teams and external health‑system partners. Required Functional Competencies: INTERPERSONAL – Develops and maintains excellent working relationships and possesses exceptional judgment ORAL COMMUNICATION - Expresses information (ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively; listens to others and responds appropriately PROBLEM SOLVING – Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations SELF-MANAGEMENT – Sets well-defined and realistic personal goals; displays a high level of initiative, effort, and commitment towards completing assignments in a timely manner; works with minimal supervision; is motivated to achieve; demonstrates responsible behavior TECHNICAL COMPETENCE – Uses or gains knowledge necessary to perform the major functions of the role as described above SYSTEMS THINKING – Understands how operations, workforce management systems, data pipelines, and analytics tools interrelate, and can design changes that account for downstream impacts WRITING – Recognizes and uses correct English grammar, punctuation, and spelling; communicates information in a succinct and organized manner; produces written information that is appropriate for the intended audience. CUSTOMER SERVICE – Demonstrates and delivers exceptional service to health system partners, patients, and internal stakeholders in a professional, courteous, accurate, complete, and timely fashion TEAMWORK/COLLABORATION – Demonstrates skills and abilities in team/project- oriented activities. RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT – Maintains good communication and a positive relationship with Team Members at all levels of the organization and all health system partner liaisons. Essential Duties and Responsibilities · Own the ongoing execution and improvement of workforce forecasting processes including generation of staffing forecasts and dissemination of forecasts into standard templates/tools for market schedulers. · Develop and implement processes and best practices for market schedulers to adhere to schedule templates and regularly optimize schedules to staff to model (e.g., trailing volume monitoring, contingent worker shift modifications, call-out strategies, etc.). · In collaboration with analytics and IT resources, define data requirements and oversee development of automated reports and dashboards that track schedule templates and staff to model adherence. · Create and distribute monthly reports on scheduling compliance and staffing to model and undertake corrective actions with market management and schedulers. · Maintain and oversee clock-in/clock-out analysis and compliance and develop processes to improve reporting and team member adherence. · Develop processes and best practices for time tracking reporting, reconciliation, and management (OT, period end processes, etc.) · Serve as a program owner and primary subject matter expert for scheduling and time tracking solutions. · Develop and maintain standard processes and best practices for use of scheduling and time tracking solutions. · Maintain a deep understanding of how forecasting, scheduling, and time tracking tools interact. Innovation: Consistently uses good judgment, applying creativity to overcome obstacles and increasing effectiveness and efficiency through process and other forms of innovation. Diversity & Inclusion: Fosters diversity and inclusion, to be able to better understand team members, our customers and partners. Engages the strengths and talents of each GoHealth team member, creating an environment of involvement, respect and connection where the richness of ideas, backgrounds and perspectives are harnessed. Makes decisions, with a focus on doing the right thing; treats team members, our customers, partners and vendors with dignity, consideration, open-mindedness and respect. Accountability: Always shows initiative, demonstrates a bias to action and gets things done. Actively accepts responsibility for diverse roles, obligations and actions that positively influence patient and customer outcomes, our partnerships and the healthcare needs of our communities. title: Implementation Manager - Data Solutions
jd_text: GoodRx is the leading prescription savings platform in the U.S. Trusted by more than 25 million consumers and 750,000 healthcare professionals annually, GoodRx provides access to savings and affordability options for generic and brand-name medications at more than 70,000 pharmacies nationwide, as well as comprehensive healthcare research and information. Since 2011, GoodRx has helped consumers save nearly $75 billion on the cost of their prescriptions. Our goal is to help Americans find convenient and affordable healthcare. We offer solutions for consumers, employers, health plans, and anyone else who shares our desire to provide affordable prescriptions to all Americans. About this Role: GoodRx is seeking an Implementation Manager - Data Solutions to join our Pharma Direct team. This role will sit at the intersection of program management, client implementation, and technical execution, with a focus on bringing complex data feeds to life for pharmaceutical and media agency partners. The ideal candidate brings strong pharmacy claims-level data expertise and hands-on experience working with claims data, with the ability to understand how claims data is sourced, structured, analyzed, and translated into external-facing products and programs. They will also work with physician-level data (PLD) and should be comfortable understanding how provider-level data is structured, matched, and leveraged. They are equally comfortable driving discovery for technical requirements, managing timelines, coordinating cross-functional stakeholders, and gathering the technical details needed to launch and scale data integrations. They bring a strong mix of pharmacy claims and physician-level data fluency, program leadership, technical acumen, and strategic prioritization, and can translate business needs into organized data execution plans across Product, Data Engineering, Analytics, Legal, Client Success, and Sales teams. This is a high-impact role for someone who enjoys building structure in ambiguous environments, driving launches from kickoff through go-live, and improving how teams deliver complex data solutions at scale. Responsibilities: Lead end-to-end launches of pharmacy claims-level and physician-level data (PLD) integrations, from initial requirements through testing, go-live, and handoff, for pharmaceutical manufacturers and media agency partners Apply strong claims data expertise to understand data sources, structures, specifications, matching, business rules, and downstream use cases, translating complex data requirements into clear implementation plans Partner closely with Product, Data Engineering, Data Analytics, Legal, Privacy, Client Success, and Sales to translate business and client needs into scalable, high-quality data solutions Serve as the central point of coordination across internal teams and external partners, keeping data feed execution aligned, dependencies visible, decisions documented, and launches moving forward Triage and drive resolution of high-priority or urgent data issues, coordinating across Client Success, Product, Data Engineering, Data Analytics and external partners to assess impact, determine next steps, and communicate status Balance standardized data specifications and scalable processes with custom client requirements, helping the organization deliver tailored solutions without sacrificing data quality or operational discipline Coordinate data-sharing requirements and contractual workflows across internal and external Legal, Privacy, and Data Security partners to ensure appropriate agreements and approvals are in place to provision data between parties Drive continuous process improvements, documentation, templates and best practices that reduce time to launch feeds Triage contractual agreements between internal and external Legal partners to provision data sharing between parties Create visual examples, workflows, or launch artifacts when needed to support stakeholder alignment and implementation clarity Partner with post-launch teams to ensure smooth handoff, reinforce KPIs, and support ongoing data optimization where needed Skills and Qualifications: Strong pharmacy claims-level data expertise, with professional experience working with pharmacy claims data in areas such as pharmacy workflows, claim adjudication, patient affordability, access programs, or healthcare analytics Experience working with physician-level data (PLD) 3 - 5+ years of professional experience in technical project/program management, implementation, technical operations, or a similar role Experience leading external-facing technical implementations, data integrations, or client-facing data solutions from requirements through launch Ability to translate business and client goals into clear technical requirements, data specifications, workflows, and execution plans Familiarity with technical concepts including data integration protocols (SFTP, S3), encryption, data transfers, file specifications, and integration testing Strong understanding of how to interpret and communicate data requirements, identify gaps or inconsistencies, and partner with technical teams to drive resolution Strong project management skills, including milestone planning, dependency and risk management, issue tracking, stakeholder coordination, and status reporting Strong written and verbal communication skills Ability to independently drive work in an ambiguous environment while also collaborating closely with cross-functional teams and external partners Experience with project tracking and collaboration tools such as Jira, Asana, Confluence, Slack, TaskRay, and Google Workspace All GoodRx employees are responsible for reviewing and complying with all Company safety and security policies and procedures, being vigilant and observant of potential security threats (including phishing attempts) and proactively communicating with the Security Team to raise any concerns. title: Project Manager
jd_text: What You'll Be Doing Job Scope: The Project Manager is generally responsible for performing all aspects of project management for moderately complex engineering project assignments ensuring total delivery of the services on time, within performance budget and quality expectations. This work will be performed under minimal supervision from our Pasadena or Angleton office. Primary responsibilities will include but not be limited to: Efficiently manage promotional projects minimizing the cost to Hargrove by working with the Engineering Resource Leaders to accurately estimate Professional Services man hours to complete the project while achieving the objectives. Successfully managing commercial contract(s) on one or more projects of various sizes, as required. Ensure that invoices are paid in a timely manner, Project Change Notices are processed, monthly Office Earnings Report (OER) is reviewed in the time allotted, and the project(s) plan in Vision is current. Maintaining control of the project by tracking and maintaining discipline performance budget progress, schedule commitments, and quality standards. Understanding and utilizing the project tools that are available for project control. Participating in development of all major technical, cost, scheduling and performance decisions on assigned projects. Familiarity with project scope, specifications, deliverables required by client, and design criteria upon assignment to a project and gaining Hargrove team alignment of schedule and budget in regard to deliverables required. Work with client team to define project scope, goals and deliverables that support business goals in collaboration with stakeholders. Recognizing and communicating scope and design changes promptly by championing the Project Change Notice process and promoting a positive Change Management culture. Leading the effort in building a productive Team both within Hargrove and with the client. Utilize rewards where applicable to recognize outstanding contributions. Coordinating resource requirements with other ongoing project work and insure all parties’ expectations are aligned. Planning and organizing the work of your team. Communicating the plan to your team, the project leadership team and the client. Aligning the expectations of all parties. Conduct weekly coordination meetings with the Team. Maintaining timely and accurate reporting including weekly and monthly reports utilizing a comprehensive action item list. Reviewing engineering documents, vendor submittals, fabrication drawings and other construction submittals for compliance with engineering drawings, specifications, good engineering practice, and project objectives. Project Manager is responsible for ensuring all documentation is reviewed and checked against vendor submittals, specifications, interdiscipline, etc. regardless of resource location. Ensuring that standard project work processes are followed by all team members through all phases of engineering, procurement, and construction. Interviewing discipline leads to maintain up-to-date progress against man hour expended analysis. Project Manager is responsible for overall financial health of each project with the respective discipline leads being responsible for producing the required deliverables within the given budget. Assessing the performance of the project team members through the course of the project, and work with resource leadership to organize a qualified and motivated project team. Ensuring project documentation is properly reviewed and approved by the client. Providing Construction Phase Support, start-up assistance, and response to Requests for Information, as needed. Managing timeliness of client team decision making and package approval. Promoting continuing positive relations with the client building on long term relationships that continue to add additional services. Completing project closeout as required by the client. Effectively and proactively managing the client needs at all stages of the project. Ideal Background Education: Bachelor or Master of Science degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical or Civil Engineering from an accredited university is preferred. Certification: Professional Engineering and/or Project Management Professional (PMP) registration is highly preferred. Experience: Requires up to 10 years of relevant experience in engineering and project management. Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: Knowledge of the Hargrove project execution procedures. Knowledge and application of company business standards and good practices. Knowledge and application of company engineering standards and project controls tools. Demonstrated proficiency in complex project management. Ability to lead a team to deliver on commitments. A comprehensive understanding of the function of all engineering disciplines, procurement, and construction processes. Ability to manage client relationships in complex situations. Ability to relate easily to others in the business community such as customers, suppliers, contractors, government, professional and trade associations. Ability to handle stress with poise. Understanding of existing and potential customer needs and preferences. Ability to delegate authority appropriately. Ability to set priorities. Demonstrated leadership ability with team orientation. Coaching and mentoring skills and experience. Excellent listening and communication skills, both verbal and written. Excellent presentation skills. Excellent leadership and organizational skills. Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office. Physical Requirements: Ability to sit, stand, or walk for long periods of time. 77034 Hargrove Culture We work to create an environment founded on trust, personal integrity, and a “team mentality” so that each person understands the value of their contributions both on a project and company-wide level. Our safety culture protects and promotes the well-being of every person who works with us and every person touched by our work. jd_text: About us HMH is a leading provider of drilling solutions, offering a wide range of products and services that are designed to be the safest and most efficient in the industry. Apart from our expertise in land and offshore operations, we are continuously expanding our knowledge within subsea mining, geothermal, onshore and offshore construction, as well as offshore wind industries. With offices in 16 countries across five continents, HMH maintains a strong global presence. HMH is a frontrunner in developing and providing automation and digital solutions for our drilling customers to support their endeavor to improve efficiency and environmental footprint. Equipped with its brilliant team of engineers, HMH is committed to actively exploring opportunities in other industries. For us, this means new opportunities and challenges that we need creativity and great minds to solve in our efforts to innovate our future. Do you want to join our team? At HMH we value our employees. We offer exciting job opportunities that will give you the opportunity to grow in your role and give you the professional development you deserve. In addition to competitive pay and benefits, you will join a casual and inclusive work environment. Our environment is based on respect and having a good day at work, so you can expect to join a knowledgeable, global team who help each other to succeed. Join Our Team Our Project Management Team is dedicated to delivering exceptional post-sales support to our global customers. We ensure seamless assistance from project initiation through to completion for subsea equipment, including comprehensive full stream packages. Our commitment includes providing expert technical support, reliable services, and promptly addressing any customer requests to ensure optimal performance and satisfaction. Role Summary As a Lead Project Manager, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring the successful delivery of projects, maintaining profitability, and ensuring utmost customer satisfaction through efficient management of project-related activities and resources. Responsibilities Project Delivery Excellence: Lead the timely delivery of services, upgrades, and new-built projects, ensuring adherence to predefined scope, timelines, and budgetary constraints. Scope Definition and Stakeholder Engagement: Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to define project scope and objectives, ensuring alignment with business goals and technical feasibility. Robust Project Planning: Develop comprehensive project plans to effectively track progress, anticipate potential challenges, and facilitate proactive decision-making. Change Management: Employ appropriate verification techniques to manage changes in project scope, schedule, and costs, while mitigating associated risks. Performance Measurement: Utilize suitable systems, tools, and methodologies to measure project performance and identify areas for optimization. Effective Communication: Regularly report project status to relevant stakeholders and escalate issues to management as necessary to ensure transparency and alignment. Client Relationship Management: Cultivate strong relationships with clients and other stakeholders, serving as the primary point of contact and ensuring their needs are met throughout the project lifecycle. Risk Mitigation: Conduct thorough risk assessments and implement proactive risk management strategies to minimize project risks and ensure successful outcomes. Vendor Relationship Management: Establish and maintain productive relationships with third-party vendors and service providers to ensure seamless collaboration and fulfillment of project requirements. Documentation Management: Develop and maintain comprehensive project documentation, including project plans, status reports, and other relevant records to support effective project governance and knowledge transfer. Skills/Requirements Bachelor's degree from an accredited university or college (or a high school diploma / GED with at least 5 years of work experience) Minimum of 5 years of experience in projects, services, or related production experience. Proven track record of managing teams to deliver project objectives. Strong understanding of project management methodologies, tools, and best practices. Excellent communication, interpersonal, and stakeholder management skills. Demonstrated ability to prioritize tasks, manage competing priorities, and adapt to changing circumstances in a dynamic environment. Proficiency in project management software/tools (e.g., MS Project, JIRA) and Microsoft Office Suite. Additional Information Must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis, now or in the future, without employer sponsorship for employment visa status No relocation assistance Location Houston, TX (JFK)

jd_text: Forming Our Future together FormFactor, Inc. (NASDAQ: FORM), is a leading provider of essential test and measurement technologies along the full semiconductor product life cycle — from characterization, modeling, reliability, and design de-bug, to qualification and production test. Everyone can make an impact here. Whether it's improving products, supporting customers, or positively influencing peers and the community, the contributions of our people matter. Shift: The regular hours for this position are day shift. Job Description: The New Product Introduction (NPI) Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) Coordinator is the primary operational link between Engineering, the Integration Team, and Manufacturing during the introduction of new products and first articles. The role owns the coordination and accurate setup of new products in PROMIS, Agile, Oracle, and related factory applications; drives the cross-functional readiness and factory-acceptance process; supports engineers in converting technical requirements into executable manufacturing flows and documentation; and trains the Manufacturing organization before product release. You will be responsible for managing system configuration, troubleshooting IT issues, and supporting the implementation of MES solutions. Key Responsibilities: Factory Application and Product Setup Own the end-to-end creation, maintenance, validation, and release of new-product and first-article setup in PROMIS, Agile, Oracle, and other manufacturing applications. Receive new-product introductions from the business unit and coordinate the initial review of existing designs, demand, product requirements, and source-factory information. Coordinate the creation and validation of manufacturing routings, operation sequences, part numbers, bills of material, product structures, revision levels, and supporting master data. Work with Process and Equipment Engineering by manufacturing area to define process steps, equipment requirements, toolsets, recipes, and required controls before creating the factory flow. Verify that each manufacturing operation references the correct work instruction, drawing, specification, recipe, material, tooling, inspection, and quality requirement. Coordinate required application changes with Engineering, Planning, Quality, Supply Chain, IT/Business Systems, and Manufacturing. Deliver high-level training and support end users, ensuring they are equipped to fully leverage the MES system. Serve as the Manufacturing interface with IT and business-system owners for PROMIS, Xsite, INFICON, and other systems needed to execute and monitor the product flow. Perform readiness checks and resolve or escalate system and data gaps before first-article or production execution. Maintain configuration alignment across PROMIS, Agile, Oracle, released engineering documentation, and the approved factory flow. NPI Coordination and Factory Readiness Coordinate the cross-functional introduction of new products from initial planning through first article, learning cycles, and manufacturing release. Develop and maintain NPI readiness plans, milestones, action registers, risk lists, and launch schedules. Facilitate NPI readiness reviews and ensure clear ownership, due dates, follow-up, and escalation of open actions. Coordinate design-for-manufacturability review and confirm that requirements are addressed before material is run. Lead the preliminary review and secure formal factory acceptance of the proposed product flow before first-article material is released. Confirm readiness of applications, materials, tooling, equipment, documentation, quality requirements, production controls, and trained personnel before execution. Coordinate first-article builds, learning cycles, and early production activity; document issues, decisions, and lessons learned and drive actions to closure. Finalize and release the approved PROMIS flow after factory acceptance and completion of required changes. Provide clear status communication to functional leaders and stakeholders. Product Data and Material Readiness Coordinate new-product bill-of-material introduction and ensure required components, consumables, and materials are identified before execution. Coordinate material changes and verify that approved revisions are reflected consistently in Oracle, Agile, PROMIS, work instructions, and production planning. Partner with Planning, Supply Chain, and Manufacturing to establish ordering requirements, stocking strategy, and appropriate minimum/maximum inventory levels for new products. Track material-readiness risks and escalate shortages, master-data gaps, or ordering constraints that could delay first articles or production release. Engineering and Documentation Support Assist engineers in preparing, formatting, routing, and releasing manufacturing work instructions and supporting documentation. Translate released engineering requirements into clear, operator-ready execution steps while preserving engineering ownership of technical content and approval. Coordinate reviews to ensure work instructions accurately reflect process sequence, recipes, materials, tooling, safety requirements, inspection criteria, queue-time limits, and reaction plans. Identify inconsistencies among engineering specifications, application data, work instructions, and actual factory execution and coordinate correction. Support document and configuration change control throughout NPI and production release. Manufacturing Training and Launch Support Develop and coordinate training plans for manufacturing supervisors, technicians, and operators prior to product release. Train the Manufacturing organization on new-product flows, application transactions, work instructions, documentation requirements, and critical quality expectations. Partner with Engineering and subject-matter experts to ensure technical training content is accurate and complete. Maintain training materials, attendance records, qualification checklists, and completion status. Provide hands-on floor support during first articles, learning cycles, and early production until the product is transferred to routine manufacturing ownership. Gather operator feedback and coordinate improvements to documentation, systems, and training. Preferred Qualifications & Experiences: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology or related field, or equivalent experience. Experience in IT, PROMIS systems, or a related industry, with hands-on experience using PROMIS MES systems. Experience creating or maintaining product data, manufacturing routings, bills of material, work instructions, or factory master data. Demonstrated ability to coordinate work across multiple functions and drive actions to completion without direct authority. Strong attention to detail, organization, follow-through, written communication, and verbal communication. Ability to understand technical information and translate it into clear manufacturing execution and training content. Ability to work effectively with engineers, technicians, supervisors, operators, planners, quality personnel, and business-system teams. Experience with PROMIS or another manufacturing execution system (MES). Experience with Agile PLM, Oracle ERP, or comparable product-lifecycle and enterprise-resource systems. Experience with Xsite, INFICON, or comparable factory monitoring and manufacturing support applications. Experience supporting first articles, engineering builds, product transfers, or factory launches. Experience in semiconductor, probe-card, electronics, medical-device, aerospace, or another controlled manufacturing environment. Experience developing or delivering manufacturing training. Working knowledge of configuration control, engineering change control, quality systems, and document-release processes.
