title: Director of Security Operations, Programs
jd_text: Who We Are International Justice Mission (IJM) is the global leader in protecting vulnerable people from violence around the world. Our team of over 1,300 professionals are at work worldwide in over 30 offices. Together we are on a mission to rescue millions, protect half a billion, and make justice unstoppable. We are a global community that cares for one another. We believe that the way we work is as important as the results we achieve. We provide professional excellence with joy and celebration to all those we serve . The Need For over 25 years, IJM has pioneered the work to protect vulnerable people from violence. 9 out of 9 times in the last decade, IJM’s Justice System Strengthening Projects have reduced slavery and violence between 50 and 85% for very large populations of people in poverty. As we grow to expand our impact to protect 500 million people from violence, w e are seeking a Director of Security Operations to serve as the principal security partner to IJM's program leadership, ensuring security considerations are embedded into program design, operational planning, survivor engagement strategies, investigative operations, and geographic expansion initiatives from the outset. This role operates from a clear mission-enabling posture. IJM's work is hard, and at times dangerous. The organization maintains a high tolerance for measured risk because the mission often requires operating in places and circumstances that other organizations may avoid. The Director of Security Operations is not a gatekeeper whose default posture is to stop or delay programs. Rather, this leader exists to help programs keep moving forward by shaping safe, practical, and risk-informed ways of operating in complex environments. Working in close partnership with program leadership, the Director identifies emerging threats, anticipates future operational requirements, and develops security frameworks that support program growth, innovation, and operational effectiveness. By maintaining early visibility into evolving casework models, survivor engagement strategies, office expansions, and new operational initiatives, the Director ensures security considerations are integrated proactively rather than applied retroactively. Success in this role is measured not by the avoidance of risk, but by the ability to help programs achieve their objectives safely, responsibly, and without unnecessary operational delay. The Director of Security Operations serves as a trusted advisor, strategic partner, and problem solver who balances mission objectives with the safety of staff, survivors, witnesses, partners, and the organization. All of this is done with a standard of excellence. This position is hybrid (onsite Tuesdays & Thursdays) if located in the Washington, DC area or remote for non-local candidates. It reports to the Vice President, Safety and Security and is only available for candidates with the right to work in the US. Responsibilities: Leadership & Management Provide strategic leadership for IJM's global Program Security function, ensuring security is fully integrated into program planning and operations and serves as a critical enabler of mission success in IJM complex program environments; Serve as a trusted advisor to senior program leaders and contribute to organizational strategy, risk management, and decision-making processes; Foster a culture of mission-enabling security, accountability, collaboration, spiritual health, and operational excellence; Lead, supervise, coach, and develop Program Security personnel as assigned; Provide security leadership during crises, critical incidents, and other high-risk operational situations affecting programs, staff, survivors, and partners; Strategy, Knowledge Development & Implementation Partner with program leadership to integrate security considerations into new program models, strategic initiatives, office expansions, and operational planning; Provide early analysis of emerging programmatic risks and opportunities to support informed decision-making; Develop and implement program security frameworks, standards, and solutions that enable programs to operate effectively in challenging environments; Maintain visibility into future program direction and operational changes to proactively prepare security capabilities and infrastructure; Contribute subject matter expertise to organizational planning, policy development, and implementation of IJM's Theory of Change; Networking & Partnership Develop and maintain strategic relationships with global and regional program leaders, survivor services leaders, legal teams, investigations teams, and operational stakeholders; Serve as the primary security point of contact for assigned programs and initiatives; Collaborate with Regional Security Directors to ensure alignment between program priorities and regional security support; Represent the Global Safety & Security Team in cross-functional planning forums, working groups, and organizational initiatives; Policies & Procedures Develop, review, and maintain program security policies, standards, protocols, and operational guidance; Ensure security considerations are incorporated into program design processes, operational planning frameworks, and organizational procedures; Recommend improvements to security governance, risk management processes, and operational standards based on emerging threats and lessons learned; Support the implementation and continuous improvement of the Field Security Operations Manual and related guidance documents ; Communication Communicate security risks, mitigation measures, and operational recommendations clearly to program and organizational leadership; Prepare security briefings, assessments, decision-support documents, and executive updates related to program operations; Facilitate rapid communication and decision-making during incidents, crises, and high-risk operational activities; Promote a shared understanding of risk tolerance and mission-enabling security throughout the organization; Training & Development Develop and deliver training, workshops, and briefings to strengthen security awareness and risk management capabilities across program teams; Provide coaching and informal mentoring to program leaders on security planning and operational risk management; Support organizational capacity-building initiatives related to staff safety, survivor protection, and program security practices; Research, Program Management & M&E Conduct security risk assessments and operational reviews for new initiatives, office expansions, investigations, survivor services activities, and other program operations; Monitor security trends, emerging threats, and operational risks that may impact program effectiveness; Evaluate the effectiveness of security measures and recommend adjustments to support program objectives ; Support after-action reviews, lessons learned processes, and continuous improvement initiatives following significant incidents or operational activities; and Participation in IJM’s community of spiritual formation . Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Security Management , Criminal Justice, International Relations, Risk Management, Emergency Management, Law Enforcement, Military Studies, or a related field; Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in security, risk management, humanitarian operations, law enforcement, military service, international development, or a related field; Minimum of 5 years of leadership experience managing complex security operations or risk programs; Demonstrated experience conducting security risk assessments and developing mitigation strategies in high-risk environments; Experience supporting investigations, legal operations, survivor-centered programming, or other sensitive operational activities; Experience working in international or cross-cultural settings; Demonstrated expertise in program security risk management, security risk assessment, and mitigation planning; Experience supporting program operations, survivor protection, field security, and duty of care initiatives; Experience providing strategic security advice and executive-level risk communication; Experience designing and delivering security training and capacity-building programs; Experience developing security policies, governance structures, and operational frameworks; Demonstrated capability in crisis management, incident response, and business continuity planning; Experience conducting intelligence analysis and threat assessments to support operational decision-making; Ability to lead across functions and coordinate effectively within complex, matrixed stakeholder environments; Experience leveraging security technology and travel risk management systems to support organizational objectives ; Advanced degree in a related field; Professional certifications such as CPP, PSP, PCI, CSMP, ISO 31000 Risk Management, or equivalent; Experience supporting anti-trafficking, human rights, rule of law, child protection, or humanitarian organizations; Experience working across multiple geographic regions and complex stakeholder environments; and Mature orthodox Christian faith as defined by the Apostles' Creed. C ritical Qualities: Eager commitment to IJM's Core Values: Christian, Professional and Bridge-Building; Strategic thinking and foresight; Ability to influence without formal authority; Mission-enabling mindset; Sound judgment and decision-making; Strong relationship-building and collaboration skills; Executive presence and credibility; Excellent communication and facilitation skills; Adaptability and organizational agility; Emotional intelligence and situational awareness; Integrity and stewardship; Self-starter with strong initiative; Ability to navigate ambiguity and complexity with confidence; and Commitment to excellence in service of IJM's mission. Application Process: Upload Resume, Cover Letter & Statement of Faith* in one PDF document . *What is a statement of faith? A statement of faith should describe your Christian faith and how you see it as relevant to your involvement with IJM. The statement can either be incorporated into the cover letter or submitted as a separate document and should include, at a minimum, a description of your spiritual disciplines (prayer, study, etc.) and your current fellowship or place of worship. What does IJM have to offer? Comprehensive Medical/Dental/Vision benefits Monthly commuter and parking benefits in the DC metro area Retirement benefit options Paid leave starting at 23 days 12 holidays (plus early release the day prior) Daily, quarterly, and annual community spiritual formation Robust staff care resources IJM holds strict safeguarding principles and a zero tolerance to violations of the Safeguarding Policy, Protection against Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment Policy, and Code of Ethics. Candidate selection is based on technical competence, recruitment, selection and hiring criteria subject to assessing the candidates value congruence and thorough background, police clearance, and reference check processes. At IJM, we’re committed to building a diverse workforce through fair and equitable employment practices. IJM encourages people of any race, color, age, sex, marital status or political ideology to apply for employment. While we welcome everyone into this work, we truly believe that the work we are doing is God’s work, not our own, and practice spiritual disciplines together daily. That’s why we legally require under SEC. 2000e-1 [Section702] of Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 that all employees practice a mature orthodox Christian faith, as defined by the Apostles’ Creed. I JM requires a background check, police clearance and thorough review of references with an employment offer and/or employment contract.

title: Operations Excellence Data & Information Coordinator
jd_text: Company: INEOS Oxide Interested in joining a winning team? A team whose employees share in the ownership of the business and are empowered to make a difference? Organizational context and job purpose INEOS Organization : INEOS is a global manufacturer of petrochemicals, specialty chemicals and oil products. It comprises 15 businesses each with a major chemical company heritage. Its production network spans 65 manufacturing facilities in 16 countries throughout the world. INEOS products make a significant contribution to saving life, improving health and enhancing standards of living for people around the world. Its businesses produce the raw materials that are essential in the manufacture of a wide variety of goods: from paints to plastics, textiles to technology, and medicines to mobile phones - chemicals manufactured by INEOS enhance almost every aspect of modern life. Business Context: INEOS Oxide is one of the most diverse, dynamic and successful businesses within INEOS. We operate 5 manufacturing sites in Europe and North America (Antwerp BE, Köln DE, Lavéra FR, Plaquemine US, Bayport, US). We produce a broad range of 200+ products which spread across five key value chains (Ethylene Oxide, Propylene Oxide, Oxoalcohols, Acetic Acid, and ENB), and on many of our products we are the European market leader. Our total manufacturing capacity is above 3 million tonnes per annum generating an annual EBITDA of ~300 M€. INEOS Oxide is an energetic business which is growing actively on a global level, with projects to extend our production base to new sites in North America and Asia in addition to continued investment on our existing platforms. We are committed to resourcing the Procurement team accordingly to deliver on this ambitious growth agenda. title: US Procurement Manager
jd_text: Company: INEOS Oxide Interested in joining a winning team? A team whose employees share in the ownership of the business and are empowered to make a difference? COMPENSATION NOTE: Indicative grade - Hay 37/S1, subject to job grade evaluation and candidate level of experience. Role Organizational Context and Job Purpose INEOS Organization : INEOS is a global manufacturer of petrochemicals, specialty chemicals and oil products. It comprises 15 businesses each with a major chemical company heritage. Its production network spans 65 manufacturing facilities in 16 countries throughout the world. INEOS products make a significant contribution to saving life, improving health and enhancing standards of living for people around the world. Its businesses produce the raw materials that are essential in the manufacture of a wide variety of goods: from paints to plastics, textiles to technology, and medicines to mobile phones - chemicals manufactured by INEOS enhance almost every aspect of modern life. BUSINESS CONTEXT: Ethylene oxide (EO) is an important building block for the preparation of a wide variety of EO derivatives (EODs), including various surfactants, as well as a host of other chemical intermediates including Glycol Ethers, Polyethlene Glycols, Ethanolamines, and Alkyl Alkanolamines. INEOS Oxide is one of the world’s leading producers of Ethylene Oxide (EO) and Ethylene Oxide Derivatives (EODs). We currently have a total EO and EOD capacity of 920 kta spread across five different production units throughout Europe and the US. These units have leading cost economics, due to economies of scale, state-of-the-art technology, strategic locations, etc. Our EO project in the US is targeting the fast-growing merchant EO market, building on our experience and leadership position in Europe. Purpose of the Job: The U.S Procurement Manager manages and coordinates Oxide’s U.S. Procurement team’s activities. The incumbent is expected to ensure that raw materials, technical materials, plant services, and logistics are safely and reliably secured at the lowest-possible cost, guaranteeing uninterrupted operations and superior customer service. The position requires a thorough understanding of contract law and what value the terms and conditions hold in a contract negotiation. These legal concepts include seller indemnifications, limitations of liability, warranties and guarantees (length and monetary value) and legal remedies. Most Important Internal Factors: Executing this role’s wide-ranging remit at both a tactical and strategic level will require the post-holder to interface directly with, and influence, the organisation far beyond their immediate procurement team. Board – reporting performance and agreeing procurement strategy and DOAs. Business and Product Managers – providing business and margin environment; how procurement can help lift results and improve the customer’s experience. Site Operations – understand requirements, monitor vendor performance, and provide commercial support when performance issues arise, support CFC and CAPEX target delivery. Procurement INEOS Oxide Europe and other INEOS divisions – network, share and look at leverage opportunities Most Important Internal Factors: Executing this role effectively will require a similarly wide-ranging engagement with parties in the external market: Suppliers – seek offers, launch RFQs, negotiate and align vendor deliverables with INEOS standards, pursue strategic partnership opportunities. Strong industry contacts, executive levels of major suppliers. Consultants/Market info – monitor market activities, trends and prices. RESPONSIBILITIES AND ACCOUNTABILITIES Highest level of customer service/satisfaction at the lowest possible cost via: Accountability 1: SHE Most important activities: This position – and all positions – with the INEOS Oxide organization - requires that the incumbent commit to learning, following, and practicing INEOS’ 20 Principles of Process & Behavioural Safety as applicable to the position. These Principles are posted throughout each Oxide facility. The incumbent must also commit to following INEOS’ Life-Saving rules on a daily basis. These are also posted within each Oxide facility. Ensure the procurement team’s activities comply with industry regulations, SHE requirements, hazardous materials rules, and internal governance. This includes supplier risk assessments, documentation control, and ensuring all suppliers meet safety, quality, regulatory, environmental, and SCOC standards. Accountability 2: Organization/Team Management Most important activities: Organize, lead & coach an efficient procurement team – control spend and costs. Set clear KPIs. Establish goals that provide direction and priorities on both tactical and strategic activities for direct reports that support the operational and business objectives and monitor progress towards their realization. Champion a culture where individuals are empowered to achieve and exceed, by delivering solutions that create value in the most innovative, efficient, and cost-conscious way possible. Recognize and reward achievement. Mentor and develop direct reports’ capabilities and build their category expertise; elevate the team’s analytical rigor and negotiation skill. Evaluate individual performance relative to goals. Strive for efficiency in procedures and working practices, drive continuous improvement. Recruitment of staff with required skill level. Network with other INEOS companies to improve efficiency/cost. Accountability 3: Develop and deliver procurement strategies Most important activities: Set sourcing strategy for all categories and guide negotiations that ensure delivery at lowest-possible cost on terms most favourable to Oxide; develop alternate sources and reduce single point vulnerabilities. Guide periodic market reviews, benchmarking, and renegotiation to help protect margins in volatile chemical markets. Coordinate with the businesses, operations, maintenance, and supply chain to anticipate needs and demand; ensuring raw materials, critical spares, materials and contracted services arrive on time; and preventing stockouts, reduced production levels or unplanned downtime. Accountability 4: Delegation of Authority Most important activities: Ensure that DOA is followed at all times. Accountability 5: Assist in or direct contract negotiations, review contract language. Oversee the development, negotiation, and administration of supplier contracts across all categories. Ensure adherence to company procurement policies, legal standards, regulatory requirements, and ethical sourcing practices across the team Manage contractual activity and timelines, guide contract negotiations and terms towards those most favourable for INEOS Oxide. Review contract language in detail, particularly indemnification, liability, insurance, and warranties. Ensure that contracts are developed to an execution-ready state. Skills/Competencies Level of Education & Experience in general 15+ years of front-line procurement experience within the chemical industry. Supervisory skills. title: Procurement Process Manager
jd_text: About the Role Integrity's Procure-to-Pay (P2P) function is a critical enabler of operational efficiency, financial control, and scalable growth. Our P2P organization is focused on delivering standardized, connected, and optimized processes across procurement and payables while driving a culture of continuous improvement and operational excellence. As a Procurement Process Manager, you will play a key role in ensuring all components of the Procure-to-Pay lifecycle are fully integrated, aligned, and operating efficiently. This role has a strong emphasis on operations, execution discipline, and driving efficiency across the end-to-end P2P process. You will act as a process leader and change agent, ensuring that P2P operations are streamlined, scalable, compliant, and well understood across the organization. Success in this role will depend heavily on strong stakeholder management, enabling alignment, adoption, and accountability across diverse business partners. The ideal candidate will bring deep understanding of end-to-end P2P operations and the ability to enhance performance through process discipline, data insights, and stakeholder engagement. This role requires someone who can translate operational challenges into actionable improvements, proactively identify gaps (including off-channel spend), and partner effectively across teams to drive adoption and compliance. The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated ability to identify and capture value from supplier relationships—going beyond cost savings to uncover opportunities for service improvements, innovation, and strategic partnership. They should be comfortable leveraging supplier data and performance metrics to surface actionable insights that benefit the organization. Strong stakeholder management is critical—this individual must be able to influence, communicate, and build trust across all levels of the organization while driving alignment and results. The successful candidate will be a proactive problem solver with a continuous improvement mindset, strong operational rigor, and a focus on delivering measurable efficiency gains. Key Responsibilities Operational Excellence & Process Efficiency Drive efficiency and effectiveness across all Procure-to-Pay operations. Ensure seamless integration and connectivity across requisitioning, purchasing, invoicing, and payment processes. Establish and reinforce standardized processes and best practices. Stakeholder Management & Engagement Build and maintain strong relationships with Procurement, AP, Finance, and business stakeholders. Act as a trusted partner and primary point of contact for P2P operational topics. Drive alignment, accountability, and adoption of P2P processes across the organization. Lead stakeholder communication, ensuring clarity and consistency. Training & Educational Activities Develop and deliver training programs to improve user adoption and compliance. Continuously reinforce process adherence through education and engagement Supplier Value Management Identify and capture value from supplier relationships beyond cost—including service quality, innovation, risk mitigation, and strategic partnership opportunities. Develop and maintain supplier scorecards and performance frameworks to drive accountability and continuous improvement. Collaborate with category managers and business owners to maximize the value delivered through supplier engagements. Recommend and implement strategies to improve spend control and visibility. Performance Management (KPIs & Scorecards) Monitor, and report key operational KPIs. Develop and maintain stakeholder and operational scorecards. Design and deliver proactive reporting that surfaces trends, risks, and opportunities before they escalate—enabling leadership to make informed decisions with timely, forward-looking insights. Collections & Account Management Maintain regular contact with customers to ensure accounts receivable remains current. Job Description Position Summary The Sr. Analyst, Demand Planning Channel Lead is an individual contributor within the Demand Planning team, reporting directly to the Director, Consensus Demand Planning. This role serves as the senior demand planning subject matter expert for an assigned channel, leading the development of demand planning methodologies, driving strategic forecast improvements, and influencing cross-functional decision making that impacts inventory, service, and financial outcomes across the enterprise. This role serves as the subject matter expert on their channel's demand dynamics, translating external signals, and near-term order patterns into forecast inputs that improve the accuracy and reliability of the consensus plan. This role requires both analytical depth and strong cross-functional partnership skills; this individual must be comfortable working inside Kinaxis Maestro and engaging with cross functional stakeholders to build the alignment that a credible consensus forecast requires. Key Responsibilities Market Intelligence & Enrichment Own the process of identifying, evaluating, and incorporating external demand-side signals for the assigned channel into the statistical baseline forecast, including macroeconomic trends, payer policy changes, healthcare system dynamics, and geopolitical disruptions that could materially affect product demand. Monitor the external environment on an ongoing basis for the assigned channel, proactively surfacing signals that warrant a forecast adjustment rather than waiting for downstream teams to flag the impact. Ensure all enrichments are documented and traceable so that forecast decisions can be explained, audited, and used to improve future enrichment quality over time. Lead the development and continuous improvement of demand enrichment methodologies, standards, and governance practices across demand planning. Evaluate emerging market trends and industry developments, translating insights into forecasting strategies and planning assumptions. Provide guidance and consultation to planners and business partners regarding the interpretation and application of external demand signals. Long Range Consensus Forecasting Own the channel-level demand inputs into the long-range consensus forecast, aligning signals from cross functional partners into a single agreed-upon view in Kinaxis Maestro for the assigned channel. Extend the planning horizon beyond near-term views for the assigned channel, ensuring that forward-looking demand assumptions are reflected in the consensus plan and available to support supply and inventory decisions across a meaningful planning window. Maintain active relationships with cross functional partners for the assigned channel, ensuring that demand-relevant intelligence is flowing into the planning process on a timely and structured basis rather than arriving ad-hoc. Facilitate resolution of complex cross-functional demand planning issues where business priorities, supply constraints, and forecast assumptions require executive-level alignment. Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance forecast accuracy, forecast efficiency, and planning capabilities across the broader organization. Represent Demand Planning in strategic planning discussions and provide recommendations that influence long-term inventory and capacity decisions. Prepare channel-level demand assumptions packages that are ready for presentation in S&OP reviews facilitated by the COE, ensuring the framing is clear and the key assumptions are visible to cross-functional participants. Demand Sensing Monitor short-term order patterns, shipment data, and near-real-time demand signals for the assigned channel to identify deviations from the statistical baseline that require immediate forecast adjustment. Refine near-term forecasts on a rolling basis using demand sensing inputs, reducing the lag between market reality and the plan without waiting for the next monthly consensus cycle. Apply clear thresholds for when a demand sensing signal for the assigned channel is material enough to trigger an off-cycle forecast update versus being held for the next scheduled planning cycle. Ensure near-term demand sensing outputs for the assigned channel are visible and actionable in the weekly S&OE cycle, flagging operationally significant deviations before they create inventory or service risk. Develop and refine demand sensing frameworks, exception management criteria, and planning best practices used across planning teams. Anticipate emerging risks and opportunities by identifying demand pattern shifts before they materially impact business performance and proactively recommend mitigation strategies. Leadership & Influence Serve as a mentor and resource to planners and analysts across the organization. Lead cross-functional projects and planning initiatives that drive business transformation and capability enhancement. Influence planning decisions through expertise, data-driven recommendations, and strong stakeholder management. Support the development of planning standards, tools, training materials, and best practices. Minimum Requirement Degree or equivalent and typically requires 7+ years of relevant experience. Education Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Data Analytics or related field, or equivalent experience. Critical Skills 7+ years of experience in demand planning, supply chain analytics, forecasting, inventory management, or related disciplines with demonstrated ownership of highly complex forecasting processes and cross-functional planning initiatives. Translating external market intelligence into credible, well-documented forecast enrichments that improve consensus plan accuracy for the assigned channel. Functional proficiency in Kinaxis Maestro or a comparable advanced planning system. Demonstrated ability to incorporate external market signals into a quantitative forecast, including the judgment to assess signal credibility and document enrichment decisions. Strong analytical skills: able to interpret forecast error metrics, identify demand patterns, and translate findings into clear, actionable recommendations. Proven ability to work cross-functionally with Commercial, Supply Planning, and Finance stakeholders to build alignment on forecast assumptions. Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Data Analytics, Business, or related field required. Building and maintaining cross-functional relationships that ensure demand-relevant intelligence reaches the planning process on time and in a usable form. Applying sound judgment on when to adjust the statistical baseline and when to hold a signal as a risk assumption, maintaining the integrity of the consensus forecast. Operating with precision and discipline inside Kinaxis Maestro, ensuring that channel-level inputs are accurate, traceable, and aligned with governance standards. Balancing near-term demand sensing with long-range forecast ownership, managing both horizons without sacrificing quality on either. Ability to influence decisions across multiple functions and levels of leadership. Demonstrated expertise designing and improving forecasting methodologies and planning processes. Ability to lead complex initiatives in ambiguous environments with limited direction. Position Summary The Sr. Analyst, Customer Facing Demand Planning sits within the demand planning organization, part of the Supply Chain Inventory Planning team and serves as the primary owner of customer–level demand execution for assigned accounts. This role reports to the Director of Customer Facing Demand Planning. They execute the customer-specific demand remit for the assigned accounts, managing inventory positioning, and service levels at the account level, while capturing and qualifying inbound demand signals including new product launches, and translating that customer intelligence back into the consensus planning process. Key Responsibilities Customer Demand Execution Maintain the customer portfolio for assigned accounts, managing formulary changes, product switches, and customer-specific inventory positions to ensure the customer-product data feeding into demand planning accurately reflects current program commitments and account relationships. Own sequestration for assigned accounts, creating and maintaining inventory buckets, assigning the correct customer accounts to each program, and coordinating with DC inventory teams to move product and discontinue sequestered item numbers as needed. Execute customer-specific award switch management for assigned accounts, updating the demand signal, adjusting the forecast for outgoing items, loading anticipated demand for incoming items, and coordinating with key stakeholders to confirm timing before transitions go live. Manage new customer onboarding for assigned accounts, including tracking, analysis, inventory builds, allocation planning, coverage reporting, SL queries, and omit analysis to ensure readiness for go-live. Manage customer-facing calls and relationships within the context of customer demand for assigned accounts, handling ad-hoc inquiries, SL questions, and contractual requirement tracking to ensure compliance and customer satisfaction. Demand Signal Intake & Translation Capture and qualify demand intelligence from assigned accounts, translating customer-specific signals including new product launches, promotional activity, program changes, and account-level shifts into structured forecast inputs, operational rules, and purchasing inputs that are consumable by the consensus demand planning team. Monitor and manage upstream demand inputs for assigned accounts, including program changes, new launch items, promotional activity, and customer-specific shifts, ensuring they are captured proactively and reflected in the plan before they create a supply risk. Own the handoff of enriched demand signal inputs from assigned accounts to the consensus demand planning team, ensuring inputs are complete, documented, and delivered on time within the monthly planning cycle. Maintain an active working relationship with the consensus demand planning team, ensuring demand signal inputs for assigned accounts are understood, accepted, and incorporated into the consensus forecast without delays or misalignment. Service Level Reporting & Analytics Create, publish, and monitor service level reports for assigned accounts, provisioning SL tracking metrics and ensuring that performance data is accurate, timely, and actionable for both internal planning teams and customer-facing stakeholders. Conduct root cause analysis on service level escalations for assigned accounts, identifying precipitating events, distinguishing supply-side from demand-side causes, and providing education and context to sales teams and customers to support sell-side conversations. Create queries and reports from multiple data sources to support data-driven decisions for assigned accounts, producing dashboards and insights that drive adjustments and surface emerging service risk before it becomes a customer issue. Process Improvement & Project Management Lead process improvement initiatives within the assigned account set, owning at least one project per year focused on improving demand accuracy, customer experience, or operational efficiency within the team. Define and maintain templates, forms, and intake documentation for assigned accounts, reducing email churn and rework by ensuring that requests from customers and internal partners arrive in a structured, actionable format. Identify and escalate process gaps or systemic friction points within the assigned account set to the Director, providing a clear description of the issue and a recommended solution. Minimum Requirement Degree or equivalent and typically requires 7+ years of relevant experience. Education Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Data Analytics or related field, or equivalent experience. Critical Skills Functional proficiency in Kinaxis Maestro or comparable advanced planning system. Strong analytical and structured problem-solving skills. Demonstrated experience managing customer programs, sequestration models, or high-touch account relationships. Managing a high-volume, operationally intensive account portfolio with precision, ensuring that customer commitments, program changes, and demand signal inputs are handled accurately and on time. Translating customer intelligence into structured, high-quality demand signal inputs that improve forecast accuracy and reduce supply risk for assigned accounts. Conducting root cause analysis on service level misses with enough depth and accuracy to equip sales teams and customers with credible, well-framed explanations. Building and maintaining trusted relationships with customers and cross-functional partners while maintaining the objectivity required to challenge demand signals that do not reflect system or market reality. Adapting quickly to new system capabilities and ways of working, including Kinaxis Maestro, and maintaining execution quality on assigned accounts through the transition. Additional Skills Experience managing sequestration programs, or high-touch strategic customer inventory models is a strong plus. Experience managing customer onboarding processes. Comfort managing a high volume of concurrent account activities with precision, prioritizing effectively when multiple issues require simultaneous attention. title: Senior Computer Vision Engineer
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.</p></div><h3>About the Team</h3> <p>The Counter Intrusion MSE team develops systems that provide force protection capabilities, monitoring the perimeter of secure areas, land or sea, for approaching people, vehicles, and vessels. We live in a world where security officers are increasingly overwhelmed by sensor data feeds. Our products leverage advanced sensor fusion and autonomy to seamlessly render activity in the environment to Lattice's common operating picture. This relieves operators of our system from a ton of burden and allows our customers to get more done with fewer personnel. Increasingly, Counter Intrusion MLEs are working on projects to bring customers' existing legacy security systems into the Lattice ecosystem. Key to this effort is building scalable software solutions so that we can service many customers without requiring bespoke software for each one. The Counter Intrusion team is responsible for the development, testing, deployment, and sustainment of our family of systems. We work closely with other teams from product, engineering, sales, logistics, operations, and mission success.</p> <h3>About the Role</h3> <p>We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to apply the latest research to solve our toughest problems. This role will be responsible for owning the whole machine learning stack for the Counter Intrusion team. You will design and train multi-sensor object detection models for perception on edge compute devices that push the boundaries of what's possible with our sensors. You will develop learning algorithms to optimize the behavior of autonomous systems. You will also be responsible for the end-to-end design, implementation, and performance of the ML stack, including the infrastructure for data collection and training. Your work will directly impact Anduril's ability to deliver cutting-edge defense technology, with the opportunity to identify and develop novel ML applications across our product portfolio.</p> evaluating performance and comparing performance trends over time</li> <li>Provide technical mentorship to other junior ML engineers</li> </ul> <h4>Required Qualifications</h4> <ul> <li>MS or PhD in detailed reports</li> <li>Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance</li> </ul> <h4>Preferred Qualifications</h4> <ul> <li>Experience in one or more of the following:</li> <ul> Minimum of 3 years’ experience as a veterinary practitioner, including internships, co-ops, and/or residency, with a preference for small or companion animal practice. Exceptional scientific communication and presentation skills, capable of engaging diverse audiences effectively. Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, PowerPoint, Teams, and OneNote. Self-motivated and able to work independently with minimal supervision. Willingness and ability to travel extensively—up to 75% within the assigned territory—with eligibility for a company vehicle; travel may include airline, train, or other modes of transportation. Develop KOL Networks: Establish and nurture a network of Key Opinion Leader (KOL) Royal Canin advocates and potential speakers within the territory, supporting veterinary operations, marketing, corporate communications, and scientific communications initiatives. Manage Territory Coverage: Adapt to territory and regional coverage requirements as needed; anticipate travel 3–4 days per week, with one day allocated for remote home office work. title: Senior Controls/PLC Technician
jd_text: Job Description: Job: Senior Controls/PLC Technician Location: Mars Petcare (Temple, Texas) Shift: Day based: Monday – Friday 8am – 5pm; on call support 24/7 Mars Petcare is seeking a PLC Technician to join our exciting pet food business at a manufacturing plant in Temple, Texas. We focus our attention on the unique needs of cats and dogs. That obsession with detail allows us to deliver precise, effective nutrition and help them become their magnificent best. As part of our overall total compensation package, Mars Petcare offers a competitive benefits package to all associates: Medical, Dental, Vision & Life Insurance, Short- & Long-Term Disability, and 401k match. Associates are also immediately eligible (based on hire date) for up to three weeks of vacation, 11 Paid Holidays per year, Sick Pay, Maternity & Parental Leave, and annual bonus earning potential, plus many other ancillary benefits not listed here. The Senior Controls Technician is responsible for the efficient, safe, and reliable operating condition of the site manufacturing control and electrical systems. The Senior Controls Technician must be multi-skilled to manage, maintain, and troubleshoot site’s electrical power systems, instrumentation, motor controls, PLC, HMI, data systems, and factory control infrastructure (servers, PC’s, and networks). Additionally, the Senior Controls Technician also directs the modification and installation of control systems and facilitates the transfer of knowledge of control systems and electrical projects. The Senior Controls Technician is responsible to identify, prioritize, plan, and execute day-to-day activities with little or no supervision. Responsibilities could include the technical development of other Controls Technicians. Key Responsibilities: Identify and recommend changes to improve plant performance utilizing existing or new control systems. Make program modifications in PLC’s logic, HMI’s programs, and servo controller logic to improve equipment performance. Troubleshoot machine breakdowns and malfunctions utilizing a working knowledge of control system programs and tools required to troubleshoot PLC’s, HMIs, and VFD/servo systems including electrical schematics, programming software, meters, and other electrical test equipment. Train and assist technicians to troubleshoot, repair, replace and commission all electrical control devices including AC drives, DC drives, Servo Controllers, contactors, motors, breakers, solenoids power supplies and indicator lights. All PLC/HMI hardware including processors, discrete and analog I/O cards, power supplies, network adapters, I/O hardware, and operator interfaces, Act as technical resource to operations, maintenance on controls related issues. Assist operations and maintenance associates to meet daily priorities, coverage, and special projects. Execute to KPI’s related to Factory Controls & IT infrastructure, Services and Solutions to include Performance, Availability and Functionality Metrics Prepare job aids, user documentation, systems documentation, standard operating procedures, and training materials for plant automation systems. Key Functional Skills/Knowledge Owner of the Factory Controls & IT Infrastructure in assigned area Accountable for Implementation of Factory Controls & IT Projects Supervise the work activities of outside contractors, controls technicians, and other associates with the installation of instrumentation, PLC based control systems, and PC based operator interfaces Interact with Maintenance Department in order to solve/define Improvements Engage in Regional and Global Factory Controls & IT Infrastructure related Projects if necessary Oversee/Execute Engineering Projects by overseeing the design of control systems utilizing standardized design methodologies Minimum Qualifications: 2-year Technical Degree (Electrical/Electronic/Controls/Automation) OR equivalent experience 3 - 5 years Factory Controls & IT experience, including production system troubleshooting and problem resolution Possess or can obtain Operational Electrical Qualification Certificate (must be able to work independently on live electrical panels) Working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Microsoft PowerPoint, and Microsoft Excel Server Administration knowledge Virtual Infrastructure Administration knowledge Equipment Architecture knowledge Knowledge of databases such as Microsoft Access, Microsoft SQL Server, and database connectivity using ODBC and Wonderware, Rockwell, Siemens, or equivalent automation software Working knowledge of AutoCAD and SolidWorks PDM Good understanding of interfacing with PLC's, scales, display devices, and any other controls-related devices Understanding of networks Preferred Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Electrical/Electronic/Controls/Automation) 6 - 10 years of Factory Controls & IT experience About Mars, Incorporated Mars is a family-owned business with over a century of history, making diverse products and offering services for people and the pets people love. With almost $35 billion in sales, the company is a global business that produces some of the world’s best-loved brands: M&M’s®, SNICKERS®, TWIX®, MILKY WAY®, DOVE®, PEDIGREE®, ROYAL CANIN®, WHISKAS®, EXTRA®, ORBIT®, 5™, SKITTLES®, UNCLE BEN’S®, MARS DRINKS and COCOAVIA®. Mars also provides veterinary health services that include BANFIELD® Pet Hospitals, Blue Pearl®, VCA® and Pet Partners™. Headquartered in McLean, VA, Mars operates in more than 80 countries. The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency and Freedom – inspire its more than 100,000 Associates to create value for all its partners and deliver growth they are proud of every day. Mars is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. If you need assistance or an accommodation during the application process because of a disability, it is available upon request. The company is pleased to provide such assistance, and no applicant will be penalized as a result of such a request.

This role tunes agent prompts, intents, conversation flows, and the knowledge they retrieve so that agents respond accurately, consistently, and in the McKesson voice across email, chat, and voice. This is a hands-on operator role inside the Agentic Service Experience pillar. The Tuner adjusts the agent every day; reading transcripts, testing changes, curating the agent-facing knowledge base, and shipping iterations in partnership with Sierra and McKesson Technology. They translate the AI Agent Product Manager's prioritized backlog into actual agent behavior and translate quality findings from the AI Performance & Quality Analyst into prompt, flow, and knowledge changes. This is a new role created as part of CxO's agentic service operating model and will help shape how agent tuning and knowledge curation scale through FY27 and beyond. Key Responsibilities AI Knowledge Authoring Author and structure prompt-aware content for AI agents. Write knowledge so agents respond accurately and empathetically without hallucinating. Decide where the agent needs no additional content, where it needs context, where it can pull data from upstream systems, and where it needs detailed instructions. Tailor knowledge accordingly. Incorporate knowledge from across NAPS. Pull domain expertise from SMEs across service delivery teams into the agent knowledge base so agents respond to real customer scenarios, not just documented ones. Author in the McKesson voice. Ensure agent responses are brand-aligned, empathetic, and appropriate for healthcare and pharmaceutical customers. Partner with brand, communications, and Responsible AI partners on tone and standards. AI Information Architecture Ensure content is relevant, accurate, current, non-conflicting, and succinct. Identify gaps in content that cause agents to provide wrong answers or fail to help and fix them quickly. Optimize knowledge for retrieval. Clean up metadata, improve vector match probabilities, and decide how to chunk knowledge so retrieval is accurate and efficient on latency and cost. Treat the knowledge base as a system the agent reasons over, not a document library. Maintain knowledge freshness. Establish review cadences, last-verified dates, and removal protocols. Stale knowledge in an agent KB becomes a confident wrong answer; manage it accordingly. AI Performance Tuning Analyze failed AI conversations to identify knowledge gaps. Read transcripts, listen to calls, and read latency and accuracy logs to see where the agent “got lost” in the knowledge base. Update documentation or metadata to improve future performance and validate the fix worked. Optimize retrieval accuracy and response crafting. Use working knowledge of the Sierra tech stack to ensure responses are crafted according to segmentation requirements and decision logic across customer groups and channels. Feed back to content owners. Provide feedback to the human-facing KB owners and content standards teams when their standards or content are hindering agent performance, and partner on resolution. Product Thinking and Experimentation Provide feedback to product and engineering. Inform the AI Agent PM and McKesson Technology on prompt improvements and platform enhancements needed for authoring effective agent knowledge. Operate in an agile fashion to adapt to a rapidly changing AI ecosystem. Experiment with knowledge approaches. Lead use case evolution by experimenting with options to decide how much deterministic knowledge is necessary versus where to depend on LLM reasoning. The right answer is different for different intents, customer groups, and risk levels. Minimum Requirement Degree or equivalent and typically requires 7+ years of relevant experience. Education Bachelor's degree Critical Skills 7+ years of experience in Technical Writing, Information Architecture, Conversation Design, Knowledge Management, or Product Operations. 1+ year of demonstrated hands-on work with AI knowledge for a deployed conversational or agentic AI system. Demonstrated experience authoring structured content for technical or digital systems with the ability to author in a defined brand voice and translate ambiguous human guidance into precise, machine-actionable content. Analytical mindset with attention to precision and clarity; able to read transcripts, latency, and accuracy logs to diagnose where the agent failed and why. Excellent collaboration skills with both technical (product managers, engineers, data scientists) and non-technical stakeholders (frontline supervisors, SMEs, Legal, brand). Experience working in environments with evolving requirements and limited established processes. This role is shaping how the work gets done, not following an established playbook. Preferred Qualifications Experience working with leading LLMs (e.g., Claude, GPT-4, Gemini) and Gen AI concepts including RAG, agentic AI, chain-of-thought prompting, decision flows, and AI reasoning. Direct experience with the Sierra platform or a comparable agentic AI platform deployed at enterprise scale. Systems thinking: ability to identify downstream implications of knowledge gaps and judgment around edge cases, ambiguity, and exception handling. Understanding of semantic precision in the AI context. Experience managing knowledge bases or content systems (e.g., KM platforms, CMS tools) Contact center, customer service, or BPO domain experience in healthcare, life sciences, or regulated industries. Prior experience as a contact center agent, trainer, QA analyst, or knowledge base owner before moving into AI. Familiarity with responsible AI principles and risk considerations for regulated customer interactions. Familiarity with SQL, Python, or JSON is a plus. A documented tuning backlog is being worked on a predictable cadence, with each change traceable to a transcript, QA finding, or prioritized roadmap item. The AI Performance & Quality Analyst reports that observed quality issues are being triaged and resolved through a clear feedback loop. The AI Agent PM has a reliable partner for translating roadmap priorities into shipped agent improvements. SMEs across NAPS report that the agent reflects their domain accurately and that the process for updating agent knowledge works. This role is a hybrid position . On the accreditation side, the Specialist supports the maintenance of URAC and ACHC accreditation across Biologics sites, including policy and SOP review, evidence collection and submission, performance measure reporting, RFI response coordination, and survey readiness activities. The position requires working knowledge of specialty pharmacy operations, pharmacy claims adjudication, PBM provider manuals and state pharmacy audit regulations, and/or accreditation standards and evidence requirements. BUSINESS LICENSE ANALYST Indirect Tax | Position Description POSITION SUMMARY The Business License Analyst supports McKesson’s U.S. business license and related business tax compliance across a complex, multi-entity and multi-jurisdictional environment. A primary purpose of this position is to support practice management licensing and compliance needs, in addition to regular business license responsibilities. The role researches requirements; prepares registrations, renewals, returns, and payments; maintains accurate compliance records; and partners with internal teams and government agencies to resolve issues. The Analyst also supports audits, practice management activities, acquisitions, operational changes, and process improvements. Position Responsibilities • Research and apply state and local statutes, ordinances, regulations, agency guidance, forms, and filing instructions to determine licensing and related business tax requirements. • Prepare and submit accurate and timely license applications, renewals, amendments, closures, business tax returns, supporting schedules, and payments. • Determine filing requirements by analyzing legal entities, business activities, locations, products and services, revenue streams, sourcing, and jurisdictional thresholds. • Maintain the business license compliance system and complete records of account numbers, filing frequencies, due dates, payments, licenses, applications, returns, correspondence, and workpapers. • Monitor deadlines and notices, resolve account issues with licensing and taxing authorities, and promptly escalate potential late filings, penalties, missing information, or compliance exposure. • Coordinate with third-party business license administrators to communicate requirements, provide data and documentation, monitor filing and renewal activities, resolve issues, and confirm timely completion. • Prepare clear, organized, and audit-ready workpapers documenting data sources, calculations, research, conclusions, approvals, filings, and payments. • Partner with Tax, Legal, Finance, Accounting, FP&A, Real Estate, Facilities, Regulatory, IT, and business operations as necessary to obtain information and implement practical compliance solutions. • Support acquisitions, dispositions, reorganizations, new affiliates, facility openings and closures, and operational changes by identifying and coordinating licensing and business tax requirements. • Maintain knowledge of assigned businesses, develop and follow standard operating procedures and controls, and identify opportunities to improve compliance through technology, automation, data analytics, and approved AI tools. • Support practice management by coordinating The McKesson Pentest Team is seeking a Penetration Testing Engineer to help support and scale McKesson's Continuous Adversarial Testing (CART) program and strengthen the security posture of our enterprise application ecosystem. This role provides technical support for offensive security programs, focusing on AI-enabled security testing, web application penetration testing, cloud security assessments, vulnerability validation, and adversarial testing across large-scale application portfolios. The individual in this role will partner with a pentest lead, engineering, product, cloud, and security teams to identify complex attack paths, validate threats, and drive remediation efforts that reduce business risk. The position will play a key role in executing autonomous security testing capabilities, integrating CART outputs into security operations, and advancing McKesson's offensive security assessments. This role will also help shape the future direction of AI-assisted security testing, automation, and modern offensive security methodologies across the enterprise. This is a hands-on technical role for someone who can support the development of a new security program while also performing advanced technical testing, validating AI-generated findings, solving operational challenges, and supporting the long-term direction of McKesson’s offensive security capabilities. Support and help shape the first iteration of the CART operating model. Execute and refine repeatable onboarding processes covering application context, test accounts, authentication, authorization roles, test data, rate limits, WAF coordination, exclusions, maintenance windows, and emergency stop procedures. Perform human-in-the-loop reviewing, reproducing, validating, prioritizing, and communicating findings generated by autonomous testing platforms. Support the execution of continuous AI assisted penetration tests across high-priority enterprise web applications, including application onboarding, test orchestration, execution oversight, findings validation, and remediation coordination. Implement integrations between CART platforms and vulnerability management, engineering, reporting, and remediation workflows. Conduct AI-enabled web application, API, and cloud security assessments across enterprise environments. Perform penetration testing, adversarial assessments, and vulnerability validation activities against internally developed and third-party applications. Evaluate emerging autonomous security testing capabilities and recommend changes to CART strategy, tooling, and service delivery. Contribute to program documentation including; playbooks, runbooks, technical standards, training materials. Leverage automation and AI-assisted security tooling to scale testing coverage and improve assessment efficiency. Identify and validate complex attack paths involving authentication weaknesses, authorization flaws, business logic vulnerabilities, and multi-stage exploitation scenarios. Evaluate REST APIs, GraphQL APIs, cloud-native architectures, and modern authentication technologies. Partner with engineering teams to explain findings, prioritize remediation efforts, and validate fixes through retesting. Develop and maintain testing methodologies, automation workflows, and security assessment procedures. Contribute to incident investigations, threat modeling activities, and continuous security improvement initiatives. Basic Requirements 4+ years of cybersecurity, application security, penetration testing, offensive security, or related experience. Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience. Experience performing web application and API penetration testing. Experience validating security vulnerabilities, assessing exploitability, and distinguishing actionable findings from false positives. Experience assessing enterprise applications utilizing REST APIs, GraphQL APIs, authentication systems, and cloud-native technologies. Working knowledge of AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP) security concepts. Experience documenting technical findings and communicating remediation guidance to engineering teams. Hands-on experience with Burp Suite Professional, Nuclei, Nmap, Metasploit, Postman, and Kali Linux tools. Preferred Skills/Experience Experience leveraging AI-assisted security tools and security automation platforms. Experience implementing, operating, or scaling continuous security testing, attack simulation, breach and attack simulation, or automated offensive security capabilities. Experience evaluating, validating, and triaging findings from automated or AI-assisted security testing platforms. Experience assessing AI-enabled applications, agent-based systems, LLM integrations, or AI security risks. Familiarity with DevSecOps, CI/CD security controls, and secure software development practices. Knowledge of OWASP Top 10, API Security Top 10, threat modeling, and secure design principles. Experience conducting red team, adversarial simulation, or attack path validation exercises. Knowledge of cloud security architecture and containerized environments. Experience performing cloud security assessments in AWS, Azure, and GCP environments. Experience creating custom security testing scripts and automation workflows. Experience developing proof-of-concept exploits and adversary emulation scenarios. Familiarity with security control validation and compliance frameworks. Experience mentoring engineers and contributing to security program maturity. Experience supporting regulated industries such as healthcare, finance, or other highly regulated environments. This role plays a critical part in delivering high-quality pharmacy services while balancing operational performance, customer expectations, financial goals, and compliance requirements. What You'll Do • Lead the day-to-day operations of a specialized pharmacy, including pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, supervisors, leads, and support staff. • Serve as the Pharmacist-in-Charge and maintain compliance with all applicable federal and state pharmacy regulations, Board of Pharmacy requirements, licensing standards, PDMP requirements, and internal policies. • Oversee prescription processing, medication preparation, dispensing, labeling, storage, inventory management, recalls, expiration controls, order fulfillment, and patient delivery activities. • Support Direct-to-Patient and Free Goods programs while ensuring operational accuracy, quality, and patient safety. • Ensure operational readiness through workforce planning, scheduling, staffing, training, and business continuity planning. • Recruit, onboard, coach, develop, and manage team members while building leadership capability and succession plans. • Establish and maintain SOPs, workflows, operational controls, training programs, exception processes, and documentation standards. • Monitor and improve key performance indicators, including prescription quality, service levels, productivity, patient experience, customer satisfaction, and program SLA performance. • Manage departmental budgets and cost-center performance by analyzing workload volumes, staffing requirements, operational expenses, jd_text: McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. Position Summary The Sr. Analyst, Statistical Forecast & Accuracy is an individual contributor within the Demand Planning team, reporting directly to the Consensus Demand Planning Lead. This role is the technical authority for the statistical forecast that underlies the consensus plan. The Sr. Analyst is accountable for ensuring the system produces a reliable, accurate baseline forecast across portfolios, and governing forecast performance over time. This role intervenes when the engine produces outputs that do not reflect reality, manages model parameters and bias across portfolios, and drives the continuous improvement discipline that makes the consensus forecast credible and defensible. This is a technical role that requires deep proficiency in statistical forecasting methods, hands-on expertise in Kinaxis Maestro, and the judgment to distinguish a model problem from a demand reality problem. The Sr. Analyst must be able to translate statistical findings into clear, actionable guidance for the Consensus Demand Planning Lead. Key Responsibilities Statistical Forecasting & Model Governance Own the configuration and maintenance of statistical forecast parameters in Kinaxis Maestro, including model selection and parameter tuning. Apply history cleansing disciplines prior to each forecast cycle, adjusting for outliers, customer losses, NDC switches, and new product launches to ensure the statistical baseline reflects true underlying demand patterns. Intervene directly when the system produces outputs that are wrong: update model parameters, alter model selection, and document the rationale for every change so that interventions are traceable and auditable. Serve as the primary point of contact for the COE on statistical forecast configuration, parameter governance, and planning engine integrity questions. Forecast Accuracy & Bias Management Own the forecast accuracy and bias measurement framework across all portfolios, tracking MAPE, bias, and error metrics at the appropriate level of granularity to surface actionable insights rather than just headline numbers. Conduct structured root cause analysis on forecast misses, distinguishing between model failure, enrichment failure, and genuine demand variability, and communicating findings clearly to the Consensus Demand Planning Lead and Channel Leads. Identify and flag systematic bias in the statistical forecast, whether directional over- or under-forecasting by product type, channel, or time horizon, and drive model adjustments to correct it. Maintain a continuous improvement cadence, tracking accuracy trend over time and holding the team accountable to improving against a defined baseline as the system matures and data quality improves. Partner with Channel Leads to determine whether a forecast miss originated in the statistical baseline or in enrichment inputs, and prepare forecast performance reporting for S&OP reviews facilitated by the COE, ensuring accuracy findings are visible to cross-functional participants and tied to operational implications for supply and inventory. Minimum Requirement Degree or equivalent and typically requires 7+ years of relevant experience. Education Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Statistics, Data Science, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field strongly preferred or equivalent experience. Critical Skills 7+ years in demand planning, supply chain analytics, or a related field, with demonstrated hands-on experience owning statistical forecast configuration and model governance in a production planning environment. Direct experience working in Kinaxis Maestro, including parameter configuration, model selection, and demand planning engine operation. Experience in a comparable advanced planning system (SAP IBP, Blue Yonder, o9) considered with a clear expectation of rapid Maestro proficiency. Demonstrated ability to diagnose and correct statistical forecast failures, including history cleansing, outlier management, and model parameter adjustment. Proven ability to build and maintain a forecast accuracy and bias measurement framework, including root cause analysis and continuous improvement tracking. Configuring, maintaining, and intervening in Kinaxis Maestro to ensure the statistical forecast engine produces reliable outputs across all portfolios. Applying disciplined cleansing and data preparation so that the statistical baseline reflects real demand patterns rather than data noise. Diagnosing forecast failures with precision, distinguishing model problems from enrichment problems from genuine demand variability, and routing accountability correctly. Building and sustaining a bias management discipline that improves forecast quality over time rather than accepting persistent error as unavoidable. Operating as the technical anchor for a team that is otherwise oriented toward commercial and market judgment, without creating a bottleneck or a knowledge silo. Additional Skills Experience operating within a structured S&OP or consensus planning process, including preparing performance reporting for cross-functional review. Familiarity with pharmaceutical, healthcare, or wholesale distribution demand dynamics is a strong plus, particularly experience with product lifecycle events, NDC switches, and new business onboarding that create history anomalies. Comfort operating in ambiguity and building process structure where governance is still maturing, particularly in the context of a large-scale system transition where baselines and benchmarks do not yet exist. Ability to communicate technical findings clearly to non-technical stakeholders, including explaining why the system produced a wrong output and what was done to fix it. Job Description The Senior HR Enablement Specialist is a critical partner that supports the strategic execution of critical people initiatives for the collective HRBP team. They most often support VP and SVP HR Business Partners, ensuring consistent, high‑quality execution of HR programs and processes across complex business units and functions. In this role, you translate HRBP direction into strategic and operational delivery, enabling and executing cyclical HR enterprise processes, as well as organization-specific talent initiatives, preparing and synthesizing workforce insights, , executing & facilitating organizational design and change activities led by the HRBP, while ensuring consistent application of HR programs and enterprise standards. You will work within the frameworks established by HR Shared Services, Centers of Expertise, and the HR Product Operating Model, ensuring adherence to standards, applying judgement to navigate ambiguity and surfacing meaningful feedback when barriers or experience gaps arise. You need to have a deep understanding of your client talent priorities and nuances to refine, not deeply customize, delivery within your client’s structure, goals and limitations. This requires you to proactively, with limited guidance, adapt actions plans to reach desired outcomes. This role also requires growing digital and AI-enabled HR acumen, applying emerging tools to strengthen analysis, streamline delivery, and enhance HRBP support. This role is ideal for someone who excels at bringing structure to established processes, facilitating and supporting key HR discussions, aligning stakeholders, and ensuring accurate, reliable execution— knowing when to execute, when to facilitate, and when to redirect to the appropriate HR teams or expertise. About the Role: The Senior Manager, Segment Strategy - Generics is an analytical individual contributor role within the strategy team, supporting the development of frameworks, models, research and strategy recommendations that enable the evaluation and execution of key strategic initiatives for our Generics business within our North America Pharmaceutical Distribution (NAPD) segment. Reporting to the VP, Product Strategy & Strategic Initiatives, this position operates as a key strategic partner to our Generics organization.
