title: Director, Customer Facing Demand Planning
jd_text: McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care. What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you. Position Summary The Director, Customer Facing Demand Planning sits within the demand planning organization, part of the Supply Chain Inventory Planning team and serves as the primary owner of customer– level demand execution for a n assigned segment . This role leads a team of ~10 FTE and reports to the Sr. Director of Customer Facing Demand Planning . They execute the customer-specific demand remit for the assigned segment, managing inventory position ing, and service levels at the account level, while capturing and qualifying inbound demand signals including new product launches, and translating that customer intelligence back into the consensus planning process . Key Responsibilities Customer Demand Execution Manage the day-to-day customer-facing demand function for the assigned segment , ensuring the team executes against established standards a s a high-responsiveness partner to customers and cross-functional stakeholders. Maintain the sequestration and strategic customer program model for the assigned segment, ensuring inventory is accurately bucketed, program commitments are honored, and customers have reliable access to the inventory they are entitled to; oversee customer portfolio management including formulary changes, product switches, and customer-specific inventory positions. Direct the customer onboarding function for new accounts, ensuring inventory builds, allocation planning, and system setup are executed in a coordinated, go-live ready manner. Manage escalations and serve as the primary point of escalation for customer facing communication within the assigned segment , resolving service level inquiries, and ensuring contractual requirements are tracked and met, escalating to the Sr. Director when required . Ensure customer-specific award switch execution is completed accurately and on time for the assigned accounts. Demand Signal Intake & Translation Execute the demand signal intake process for the assigned segment , ensuring the team captures, validates , and enriches customer intelligence against established quality standards before passing inputs to the consensus demand planning team. Monitor and manage upstream demand inputs for the assigned segment , including program changes, new launch items, promotional activity, and customer specific shifts ensuring they are ca ptured proactively and reflected in the plan before they create a supply risk. Maintain an active working relationship with the consensus demand planning team, ensuring demand signal inputs are understood, accepted, and incorporated into the consensus forecast without delays or misalignment. Service Level Reporting & Analytics Manage service level performance for assigned segment , e nsuring the team produces accurate , timely service level reports and national tracking metrics that enable proactive management of service risk. Conduct and direct root cause analysis on service level escalations and omits for assigned accounts, holding the team accountable to identifying precipitating events and driving remediation. Maintain and improve analytical capability within the team, including dashboards, data queries, and reporting tools that surface allocation and policy decisions faster and with greater accuracy. Team Leadership, Development & Continuous Improvement Manage and develop a customer-facing demand team for assigned segment , holding team members accountable to performance expectations, role clarity, and the operating standards set by the Sr. Director. Coach and develop team members toward greater ownership and capability, providing regular feedback, identifying development opportunities, and creating visibility into advancement paths within the demand planning organization. Partner with the other Directors of Customer Facing Demand to drive continuous improvement efforts, share leading practice s and drive consistency across teams. Maintain a close pulse on team workload, capacity, and execution quality across accounts , proactively identifying resource constraints or process gaps before they affect customer service or demand signal accura cy. Minimum Requirement Degree or equivalent experience. Typically requires 12+ years of professional experience and 4+ years of management experience. Education Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain , Business or related field, or equivalent experience. Critical Skills 1 2 + years in supply chain, demand planning, or customer operations roles with at least 4 years in a leadership capacity managing teams and driving cross functional outcomes. Elevating the quality and reliability of the demand signal entering the consensus planning process through disciplined intake governance and rigorous enrichment practices. Building trusted relationships with customers and cross– functional partners while maintaining the objectivity required to make hard calls on the forecast. Managing a high volume, operationally intensive account portfolio with precision. Functional proficiency in Kinaxis Maestro or comparable advanced planning system. Demonstrated experience leading customer-facing teams in a complex, high-volume distribution, p harmaceutical environment, with direct accountability for service levels. Strong analytical and structured problem-solving skills. Proven ability to influence without direct authority across a matrixed organization. Additional Skills St rong communication sk ills - ability to re present the segment credibly in leadership forums and translate operational complexity into clear strategic framing. Experience managing sequestration programs, or high-touch strategic customer inventory models. Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally across demand planning, supply planning, and inventory management teams. Demonstrated ability to balance customer advocacy with the analytical discipline required to challenge demand signals that do not reflect system or market reality. Familiar with demand planning analytics and reporting tools, including dashboards and data queries that support account-level service level management. Physical Requirements Traditional office requirements. A large percentage of time performing computer-based work is required. Hybrid role, must live near Las Colinas office. Up to 25% travel. This role is a hybrid position . The selected candidate is expected to work on-site at our Las Colinas office a minimum of two (2) days per week , with the remaining days worked remotely. Specific in-office days may be designated based on team needs and business priorities. We are proud to offer a competitive compensation package at McKesson as part of our Total Rewards. This is determined by several factors, including performance, experience and skills, equity, regular job market evaluations, and geographical markets. In addition to base pay, other compensation, such as an annual bonus or long-term incentive opportunities may be offered. For more information regarding benefits at McKesson, please click here. title: Director FP&A-HQ & IT Operating Expense
jd_text: McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care. What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you. The Director, FP&A - HQ & IT Operating Expense provides strategic and hands-on financial leadership for Practice Management headquarters and US Oncology technology operating expense. The role owns planning, forecasting, close support, management reporting, long-range planning, and executive decision support across the full HQ and IT operating-expense portfolio. The Director connects spending, headcount, allocations, technology investments, and strategic initiatives to enterprise priorities and Adjusted Operating Profit outcomes. The Director serves as the senior finance partner to Practice Management leaders, the McKesson technology organization, and cross-functional Finance, Accounting, Strategy, Operations, and shared-service partners. The role leads a team of three direct reports and one indirect report, establishes clear priorities and review standards, and remains directly engaged in complex analyses, executive materials, governance decisions, and issue resolution. Success requires strong executive communication, disciplined financial stewardship, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to improve processes through standardization, automation, and scalable reporting. Key Responsibilities Strategic FP&A Leadership and Business Partnership Own the financial agenda for all HQ and IT operating expense, aligning resources and investments with Practice Management, US Oncology, and enterprise priorities. Advise senior leaders on financial performance, choices, risks, opportunities, trade-offs, and recommended actions; translate complex cost and allocation topics into decision-ready insights. Lead cross-functional work across Finance, Accounting, Technology, Strategy, Operations, Ontada, McKesson Technology, and other business units to resolve issues and advance shared objectives. Provide concise executive storytelling for leadership reviews, forecasts, budgets, long-range planning, strategic initiatives, and emerging business issues. Planning, Forecasting, Close, and Performance Management Lead annual budget planning, periodic forecasting, long-range planning, month-end close support, and management reporting for HQ and IT operating expense. Establish a transparent performance framework spanning employee-related expense, discretionary and semi-variable spend, technology costs, corporate and cross-business allocations, and strategic initiatives. Direct variance analysis, risk and opportunity assessment, headcount and open-role tracking, accrual and invoice review, and forward-looking scenario analysis. Ensure financial plans and reporting are accurate, well controlled, fully documented, and connected to underlying assumptions, business drivers, and Adjusted Operating Profit impact. HQ OPEX Governance, Allocations, and Cost Stewardship Lead governance for retained and allocated HQ expense, including allocation methodologies, documentation, legal and contractual considerations, leadership approvals, and implementation readiness. Develop recommendations that clarify service scope, funding mechanisms, practice cost sharing, pricing or service-fee considerations, and the financial impact of allocation changes. Challenge new and existing spend, identify savings and cost-avoidance opportunities, and facilitate prioritization and trade-off decisions within financial targets. Build durable processes for gross-to-net expense visibility, headcount and cost-center mapping, decision logs, and ongoing tracking of allocation outcomes. Technology Finance and Investment Decision Support Lead planning, forecasting, and reporting for US Oncology technology costs, including retained and practice-allocated expense, enterprise technology allocations, subscriptions, infrastructure, and strategic programs. Develop and challenge business cases for technology initiatives, including cost, benefit, timing, funding, capitalization, depreciation, practice impacts, and value-realization assumptions. Partner with Technology, Accounting, Fixed Assets, Controls, Tax, Procurement, and practice stakeholders to support disciplined financial governance for complex technology programs. Provide financial leadership for technology roadmaps, network modernization, system transitions, portfolio rationalization, and other strategic investments. Reporting, Automation, and Process Improvement Set the roadmap for scalable reporting, data governance, model documentation, dashboards, and self-service capabilities across HQ and IT Finance. Reduce manual effort and improve cycle time, accuracy, and insight through standard processes, automation, Power BI or Tableau solutions, and effective use of enterprise data platforms. Establish consistent templates, review standards, version control, and traceability for forecasts, budgets, P&Ls, allocation models, and executive materials. People Leadership and Organizational Effectiveness Lead, coach, and develop three direct reports across HQ OPEX, IT Finance, and allocations, while supporting development of the broader team. Set clear priorities, decision rights, service expectations, and review routines; balance effective delegation with direct engagement in urgent, ambiguous, or high-impact work. Build succession strength and expand team capabilities in business partnership, financial modeling, executive communication, systems, automation, and leadership. Foster an inclusive, collaborative, accountable culture that encourages thoughtful challenge, continuous learning, and sustainable ways of working. Minimum Requirement Degree or equivalent experience. Typically requires 12+ years of professional experience and 4+ years of management experience. Education Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field, or equivalent related experience. MBA, CPA, CMA, or other relevant advanced credential preferred. Critical Skills Typically 12+ years of progressive finance, FP&A, accounting, or related analytical experience, including 4+ years of management responsibility. Demonstrated experience leading planning, forecasting, close analysis, management reporting, financial modeling, and executive decision support in a complex organization. Experience partnering with senior leaders across multiple functions and influencing outcomes across organizational boundaries. Experience with operating-expense management, headcount planning, allocations, shared services, technology finance, or investment business cases strongly preferred. Healthcare services, provider economics, shared-services, or multi-entity experience preferred. Additional Skills Strategic and analytical thinking combined with the ability to work directly in detailed data, financial models, reporting tools, and executive materials. Advanced forecasting, scenario analysis, variance investigation, business-case development, and performance-management capabilities. Strong understanding of income-statement, capitalization, depreciation, accrual, and allocation concepts. Executive communication and presence, including concise written commentary, presentations, and data visualization. People leadership, coaching, prioritization, delegation, conflict resolution, and talent development. Cross-functional partnership, change leadership, sound judgment, attention to detail, ownership, and comfort operating through ambiguity. Digital fluency and a continuous-improvement mindset, including scalable reporting, automation, and responsible use of AI-enabled tools. Systems and Tools Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills required. Experience with enterprise planning, ERP, business intelligence, and data platforms such as BPC, Essbase, SAP, PeopleSoft, Power BI, Tableau, or comparable tools preferred. jd_text: It’s More Than a Career, It’s a Mission. Our people are the foundation of our success. By joining our growing team at Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI), a subsidiary of McKesson, you will have the opportunity to become part of one of the largest community-based cancer programs to advance oncology treatments and improve outcomes for cancer patients across the globe. We look for mission-driven candidates who have a desire to advance the fight against cancer and make a difference in the lives of patients diagnosed with cancer every day. Our Mission People who live with cancer – those who work to prevent it, fight it, and survive it – are at the heart of every decision we make. Bringing the most innovative medical minds together with the most passionate caregivers in their communities, we are transforming care and personalizing treatment. Through clinical excellence and cutting-edge research, SCRI is redefining cancer care around the world. As the Director of Research Site Partnerships you serve as the executive relationship owner for a portfolio of oncology research sites. You will drive site engagement, alignment, and performance through strategic partnership and a focus on clinical trial enrollment growth. You will operate as a strategic account leader, navigating complex situations, influencing outcomes, and partnering across leadership to align priorities, remove barriers, and deliver value in a matrixed environment. Your responsibilities will include: Manage a portfolio of approximately 5–6 oncology research sites, depending on complexity Serve as senior relationship owner for assigned sites Build executive-level partnerships with site leadership, physicians, research teams, and administrators Develop and maintain understanding of site strategy, capabilities, and opportunities Align enterprise strategy with site goals Drive accountability for clinical trial enrollment performance Analyze enrollment trends and identify growth opportunities Develop and track strategic enrollment action plans Promote best practices supporting accrual Monitor and report on key performance indicators Translate enterprise priorities into site-level strategies Lead sites through change and transformation Elevate trends and insights to leadership Navigate high-impact or complex situations Use negotiation and conflict resolution to achieve outcomes Coordinate with internal teams to support site needs Ensure alignment across stakeholders Represent site perspectives in leadership forums Identify opportunities to improve processes and engagement You should have for this position: Bachelor Degree required, master degree preferred Experience supporting oncology research sites and clinical trial enrollment Experience in site engagement, account management, or clinical operations Must have experience in clinical research operations Experience in oncology research Strategic relationship management skills Data analysis skills Excellent communication skills The ability to influence others Experience operating in a matrixed environment About Sarah Cannon Research Institute Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI) is one of the world’s leading oncology research organizations conducting community-based clinical trials. Focused on advancing therapies for patients over the last three decades, SCRI is a leader in drug development. In 2022, SCRI formed a joint venture with former US Oncology Research to expand clinical trial access across the country. It has conducted more than 850 first-in-human clinical trials since its inception and contributed to pivotal research that has led to the majority of new cancer therapies approved by the FDA in the past decade. SCRI’s research network brings together more than 1,300 physicians who are enrolling patients into clinical trials at more than 200 locations in 20+ states across the U.S. Please click here to learn more about our research offerings. We care about the well-being of the patients and communities we serve, and that starts with caring for our people. That’s why we have a Total Rewards package that includes comprehensive benefits to support physical, mental, and financial well-being. Our Total Rewards offerings serve the different needs of our diverse colleague population and ensure they are the healthiest versions of themselves. For more information regarding benefits through our parent company, McKesson, please click here . As part of Total Rewards, we are proud to offer a competitive compensation package. This is determined by several factors, including performance, experience and skills, equity, regular job market evaluations, and geographical markets. In addition to base pay, other compensation, such as an annual bonus or long-term incentive opportunities may be offered. McKesson Talent Advisors do not communicate with candidates via online chatrooms or using email accounts such as Gmail or Hotmail. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

The role leads Revenue Cycle Management FP&A, Revenue Accounting, and a newly established Balance Sheet Reconciliations function through three Director-level leaders. title: Technical Project Manager, Data
jd_text: It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing! We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business. LucyRx is seeking a Technical Project Manager to bring structure, clarity, and momentum to our data engineering organization. As we modernize our data platform, migrate legacy Oracle systems to the cloud, and build out Snowflake-based analytics infrastructure, the volume and complexity of incoming work is growing. This role exists to make sure that work flows smoothly: from intake and requirements through scoping, prioritization, execution, and delivery. You will be the connective tissue between business stakeholders who need data and the engineers who build it. You understand enough about data and technology to ask the right questions, push back on vague requirements, and protect the team from scope creep. You are comfortable running a standup, managing a backlog, and having a direct conversation when something is off track. You do not need to write code, but you need to understand what the engineers are building and why it matters. Role and Responsibilities Intake and Requirements Own the intake process for data engineering requests across the organization, including business intelligence, pipeline development, Oracle database work, and analytics enablement. Partner with business stakeholders in clinical operations, finance, product, and reporting to gather and define requirements with enough clarity that engineering can scope and execute without constant back-and-forth. Translate business needs into well-defined technical requirements. Push back when requirements are vague, incomplete, or likely to change mid-execution. Maintain a clear, prioritized view of incoming requests and help leadership make informed tradeoff decisions. Scoping and Estimation Facilitate scoping and estimation sessions with engineering leads. Ensure work is broken down to a level of detail that allows for reliable delivery commitments. Identify dependencies, risks, and assumptions early and surface them before work begins rather than after it derails. Maintain realistic delivery timelines that account for team capacity, complexity, and competing priorities. Delivery and Execution Own the day-to-day delivery cadence for active data engineering work. Run standups, facilitate sprint planning and retrospectives, and keep the team moving. Track progress against commitments and identify variance early. Escalate when something is at risk and propose solutions rather than just problems. Remove blockers. Whether it is a missing access credential, an unclear requirement, or a dependency on another team, you clear the path so engineers can focus on building. Maintain accurate and up-to-date project documentation including status reports, decision logs, and delivery timelines. Prioritization and Backlog Management Maintain and groom the data engineering backlog in collaboration with the Manager, Data Engineering and other stakeholders. Facilitate prioritization conversations that balance business urgency, technical dependencies, team capacity, and strategic roadmap alignment. Ensure the team always knows what they are working on, why it matters, and what comes next. Stakeholder Communication Serve as the primary point of contact for stakeholders seeking status on data engineering work. Provide proactive, clear, and honest updates. Set and manage expectations on delivery timelines. Do not over-promise and do not go silent when something slips. Build strong working relationships across the data, engineering, product, clinical, and finance teams. Prepare and present project status updates for leadership as needed. Qualifications and Education Requirements Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience. 5+ years of project management experience, with at least 3 years managing technical data or engineering projects. Demonstrated experience working with data engineering, analytics, or BI teams in a project management capacity. Strong understanding of data concepts: pipelines, ETL/ELT, data warehousing, and reporting workflows. You do not need to build these things, but you need to understand them well enough to scope and manage them. Proficiency with Agile, Scrum, or Kanban delivery frameworks. Comfortable running ceremonies, managing sprints, and adapting process to what the team actually needs. Experience with project and backlog management tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, Confluence, or similar. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. You can write a crisp status update, run a focused meeting, and have a direct conversation when something is off track. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. You keep things from falling through the cracks. Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment where processes are still being built. Preferences Experience managing projects involving Oracle databases, cloud data platforms (Snowflake, AWS, Azure), or data migration initiatives. Familiarity with modern data stack tools such as dbt, Fivetran, Airflow, or Tableau. Healthcare, PBM, managed care, or other regulated industry experience. PMP, PMI-ACP, CSM, or equivalent certification. Experience working with mixed teams of FTE and contractors. Exposure to HIPAA compliance requirements in a technical project context. Physical Requirements The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. This is a largely sedentary role; however, some standing, walking, bending, and reaching may be required. Regularly operates in an office or home office setting which involves utilizing a computer, mouse, keyboard, and occasionally operates other standard office equipment such as a printer, copier, and phone. Travel may be required by either car or airplane, or a combination of multiple modes of transportation. What We Do LucyRx is an independent, next-generation pharmacy benefits manager (PBM) transforming how healthcare works. We’re fixing what’s broken in the PBM industry by putting people first and challenging outdated norms. For too long, traditional PBMs have prioritized profit over patients, and we believe that’s just plain wrong. LucyRx offers bold, innovative solutions powered by LucyIQ, our proprietary AI platform, to deliver actionable insights that lower costs, improve care, and simplify prescription management. While we’re new to the PBM space, LucyRx is built on decades of leadership experience and a commitment to meaningful change. We’re a nimble, remote-first team with a bold mission to redefine pharmacy benefits—and we’re just getting started. What It’s Like to Work at LucyRx At LucyRx, we’re a fast-moving team dedicated to making healthcare simpler, fairer, and more effective. Joining us means being part of a dynamic, mission-driven group that works collaboratively to challenge outdated industry practices and redefine what’s possible in pharmacy benefits. We value accountability, innovation, and a relentless focus on making an impact. Here, you’ll find a supportive culture that encourages you to bring your whole self to work, share bold ideas, and grow alongside smart, driven colleagues who are passionate about fixing the PBM industry. If you’re ready to roll up your sleeves and make a real difference, we’d love to have you on our team. Salary 100,403.00 - 156,879.00

jd_text: It's fun to work in a company where people truly believe in what they are doing! This role serves as the voice of the customer and market, translating validated user problems, business objectives, product data, technical constraints, and competitive insights into clear outcomes, prioritized investments, and executable plans. As a key member of the Platform Product Management team, the Software Product Manager owns assigned software products and platform capabilities from problem discovery and business-case development through delivery, launch, adoption, optimization, and retirement. This position is accountable for establishing a compelling product vision, defining measurable outcomes, and making evidence-based prioritization decisions that improve customer value, revenue growth, retention, operational efficiency, and strategic differentiation. The Software Product Manager works closely with Product Design, Engineering, Architecture, Data, Quality Assurance, DevOps, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Regulatory, Customer Success, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Support, and regional teams. Translate validated customer problems and strategic opportunities into outcome-based roadmaps, product requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, release goals, and prioritized backlogs. Apply consistent prioritization methods and make clear tradeoffs across customer value, business impact, delivery effort, technical health, risk, and time to learning. Strong understanding of dispatch planning, freight management, shipment documentation, and logistics execution processes. Experience working with transporters, freight forwarders, customs brokers, and third-party logistics providers. Working knowledge of import/export operations, Customs regulations, DGFT requirements, Incoterms, and trade compliance practices. Strong analytical, problem-solving, negotiation, and stakeholder management capabilities. The economist's mindset Thinks in incentives: what a change makes players do, not only what it costs or earns. Reads an economy as flows: sources, sinks, inflation, and the marginal effect of each tweak. Trades short-term revenue against long-term economy health, and says which one a decision favors. Decides from data, models and experiments rather than intuition, then writes the reasoning down. What you will own Own the design of the game economy: currencies, sources and sinks, progression, and the pricing of virtual goods, with clear KPIs that show whether it is healthy. Build simulations and predictive models that forecast how content, pricing and balance changes will land before they ship. Plan, run and read A/B tests on economy and pricing changes, and turn the results into decisions. Define player segments from behavior and motivation, and tailor economy parameters to each segment. Own monitoring of economy health (player balances, inflation, source and sink ratios, conversion) and act on anomalies. Partner with Product, Design, Analytics, Marketing and Engineering so the economy supports game goals, and present recommendations to senior leadership. You own the economic guardrails (value per dollar, inflation, effect on progression); Monetization owns offer execution and revenue targets. Co-own LiveOps with the LiveOps team: you define the economy of each event (costs, rewards, pacing); LiveOps owns scheduling, configuration and QA. Help Product and Monetization make the experience-versus-revenue trade-off explicit. What we are looking for Ownership mindset; comfortable with ambiguity and switching context quickly. Background in mobile, online or social free-to-play games. Familiarity with LiveOps tooling and event operations, and a habit of working alongside a LiveOps team. You will take the roadmap from a shared responsibility across engineering leadership and make it your own — setting direction, sequencing the work, and driving it to delivery. AI Services is one of our most visible and strategically important programs. It operates as a shared service, which means our internal customers are the product teams across the insightsoftware portfolio, and our end customers are the finance and accounting professionals who use their products every day. This role is a senior individual contributor position: you will work as a peer to our chief architect and engineering manager, go deep on technical design decisions, and write the specifications, evaluation criteria, and enablement material yourself. Success requires someone who has built agentic systems in production, not someone who has only read about them. What Will You Do? Own the AI Services Roadmap: Define and maintain the strategy, roadmap, and quarterly priorities for agentic workflows, the tool and connector layer, and AI quality infrastructure. Make the trade-off calls on sequencing, scope, and technical direction, and defend them with evidence. Define Agentic Capabilities in Depth: Specify multi-step agent behavior — planning, tool selection , memory, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, fallback paths, and guardrails. Translate ambiguous business problems into agent designs that are reliable enough to put in front of finance users. Drive the Tool and Connector Strategy: Own the roadmap for our Model Context Protocol (MCP) surface and tool interfaces. Decide which insightsoftware data, actions, and product capabilities are exposed to agents and third-party assistants, and define the contracts, versioning, and access controls that make them safe to consume. Establish AI Quality as a Product Discipline: Build and own the evaluation framework for AI features — golden datasets, offline and online evals, regression harnesses, accuracy and hallucination measurement, and production observability. Set the quality bars that gate release and hold the team to them. Enable Consuming Product Teams: Treat portfolio product managers and their engineering teams as your customers. Run intake, document integration paths, publish reference implementations and adoption guidance, and measure whether teams are successfully building on AI Services rather than around it. Partner Deeply with Engineering and Architecture: Work daily with the chief architect and engineering manager on design reviews, technical trade-offs, model and vendor selection, and cost and latency management. Participate in sprint planning and refinement, and unblock the team on product decisions in hours, not weeks. Measure and Communicate Outcomes: Define the metrics that show whether AI Services is working — adoption across product lines, agent task success rates, eval scores, cost per task, latency, and incident rates. Report them to senior leadership with a clear read on what to do next. Manage AI Risk and Trust: Work with security, legal, and compliance to address data handling, model governance, auditability, and customer trust concerns before they become launch blockers. Qualifications Minimum Qualifications: 8 or more years in product management, with at least two years owning AI products as a hands-on individual contributor Demonstrated experience shipping large language model applications to production — not prototypes or internal demos Working technical fluency in agentic architectures : orchestration and planning patterns, tool and function calling, retrieval-augmented generation, context management, and prompt engineering Hands-on experience with the Model Context Protocol or comparable tool and plugin interfaces for connecting agents to enterprise systems Practical experience building or operating evaluation frameworks for AI systems, including how to construct datasets, choose metrics, and interpret results Experience delivering a shared platform or API-based service where other product teams are the primary consumers Ability to read code, reason about system design, and hold your own in architecture discussions with senior engineers Strong command of Agile delivery, with the judgment to know when process helps and when it gets in the way Ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders without formal title: Data Product Owner
jd_text: Marathon Health is a leading advanced primary care provider, partnering with employer and union plan sponsors to improve health for millions of Americans. With nationwide onsite, nearsite, and network health centers, and virtual primary care, Marathon delivers a value-based model that enhances the healthcare experience for members and providers, while driving meaningful cost savings for plan sponsors. Marathon is proud to be certified as a Great Place to Work®, reflecting the company's commitment to building an inclusive, high-trust culture where all employees can thrive. Learn more at marathon.health ABOUT THE JOB The Data Product Owner leads several cross-functional scrum teams responsible for delivering outcome-based data solutions to the business. This role is defined by the problems it solves , not the technology it uses. Whether the right answer is a Tableau dashboard, a Snowflake Cortex agent, a Python-based insight package delivered as a Streamlit portal, or a reusable component of our semantic model, the Data Product Owner is accountable for choosing the approach that best achieves the desired outcome and for guiding their teams to build it. Our stakeholders are primarily internal, though some solutions serve external audiences, and their needs evolve quickly. This person must be comfortable operating in an environment where both Technology and Product direction change, treating that change as a normal condition rather than a disruption. A major part of the mandate is enablement: building the foundational pieces — starting with a well-structured semantic model — that let stakeholders and teams across the organization build their own solutions, inside and outside of Technology. The ideal candidate is fluent in leveraging AI to accelerate how these solutions get designed, built, and maintained. ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES Own the product vision, roadmap, and prioritized backlog for a portfolio of outcome-based data solutions serving internal and external stakeholders. Lead multiple scrum teams day to day — including backlog grooming, sprint planning, prioritization, and removing blockers — while keeping teams focused on measurable outcomes over outputs. Take direction from the Director of Business Intelligence on analytics and reporting outcomes, and from the Technical Product Manager on technical and product execution, reconciling their input into a single prioritized backlog. Proactively surface conflicts in priority or direction early, and drive them to resolution rather than letting teams stall. Translate stakeholder goals into clearly defined problems, success metrics, and acceptance criteria, and validate that delivered solutions actually move those metrics. Select the right delivery approach for each problem (e.g., Tableau, Snowflake / Cortex agents, Python / Streamlit portals) based on the outcome and the audience, rather than defaulting to a preferred technology or pattern. Leverage AI and modern tooling to accelerate discovery, prototyping, development, and iteration across the teams. Build and steward foundational, reusable components — especially the semantic model — so that stakeholders and other teams can reliably build their own solutions against a trusted, governed layer. Establish and support self-service enablement, including documentation, patterns, and guardrails, so users can create their own solutions with confidence. Partner closely with Product leaders and internal stakeholders who depend on these solutions, keeping all parties aligned on priorities, tradeoffs, and delivery status. Anticipate and absorb change from both Technology and Product, adjusting priorities and communicating impacts without losing delivery momentum. Ensure solutions meet quality, security, and compliance expectations appropriate to internal and external use. Track adoption, usage, and business impact, and use those insights to continuously refine the portfolio. Define success metrics and business outcomes for all major initiatives and hold teams accountable for measuring realized value after delivery. Ensure solutions follow established release, change management, and production readiness processes. QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree in a relevant field plus a minimum of 7 years proven experience as a Product Owner, Product Manager, or similar role delivering data, analytics, or BI products, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Demonstrated success leading Agile / Scrum teams, ideally more than one team concurrently. Strong background in data and analytics, with the ability to reason about data products end to end (source to consumption). Experience in healthcare, population health, benefits administration, or related regulated industries preferred. Experience working with data governance, data quality, and master data initiatives preferred. DESIRED ATTRIBUTES Hands-on familiarity with Snowflake, including Cortex agents, Cortex Analyst / search services, and semantic views. Experience with modern analytics and delivery tools such as Tableau, Python, and Streamlit (or comparable frameworks for building lightweight portals and insight packages). Practical fluency in leveraging AI / LLMs to build, accelerate, or augment data solutions. Strong grasp of semantic modeling and the value of a reusable, governed foundation that enables self-service. An outcome-first, technology-agnostic mindset: chooses the right tool for the job and lets go of tools that no longer fit. Highly adaptable and calm amid shifting Technology and Product priorities. Diplomatic and decisive: builds trust with multiple stakeholders and makes clear prioritization calls when direction conflicts. A builder-and-enabler orientation: as motivated by helping others create solutions as by delivering their own. Curiosity and a habit of continuous learning as the tooling landscape evolves. Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, comfortable working with both Product leadership and non-technical business users. Experience managing product backlogs in Azure DevOps or similar tools. Awareness of data governance, security, and privacy considerations (experience handling sensitive or regulated data such as PHI is a plus). Comfort selecting and working across a range of delivery technologies rather than specializing in a single one. Experience operating in an environment of frequent change and ambiguity. Track record of translating business needs into prioritized, outcome-driven work and measuring results. Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in a matrixed structure, taking direction from multiple leaders while managing competing priorities. Pay Range: $110,000 - $140,000/yr The actual offer may vary dependent upon geographic location and the candidate’s years of experience and/or skill level. We are accepting applications for this position until a candidate has been selected. To apply to this position and learn more about open jobs at Marathon Health, visit our careers page.

Metrics-oriented and customer focused with an understanding of user experience and the ability to use customer feedback to inform product decisions. Strong project management skills with the ability to prioritize work, manage deadlines, and adapt to changing business needs. title: Appian Forward Deployed Product Owner
jd_text: Overview: The Wilmington Trust Institutional Services (IS) division is experiencing rapid business growth and has initiated a strategic digital transformation program. The goals of the program are to grow revenue through new and transformed digital-first trust and agency service products, to move from a product-centric to client-centric operating model, to move from market-specific to global solutions, and to dramatically lower the cost to serve. Wilmington Trust is seeking an Appian Forward Deployed Product Owner to help accelerate digital transformation across our core operations. This role is designed for an experienced product, business analysis, or transformation professional who can operate close to business users, translate operational needs into deployable digital workflows, and help lead iterative delivery in a regulated financial services environment. This role is a hybrid between a product owner, business analyst, low-code workflow designer, and AI-enabled process lead, with a strong focus on designing and configuring end-to-end workflows directly in Appian Designer. The role requires hands-on Appian experience , strong business process and analytical skills, and the ability to partner across business, operations, technology, risk, and product stakeholders to move quickly from discovery to working solutions. While working closely with individual business teams, the role will maintain a platform-first mindset by leveraging shared capabilities, reusable components, and consistent design patterns rather than creating isolated or duplicative solutions. Ideal candidates will be comfortable owning product outcomes, facilitating working sessions, writing stories and specifications, validating build quality, and using AI-assisted tools to accelerate analysis, documentation, prototyping, testing, and workflow improvement. The successful candidate will be able to work forward-deployed with business teams while maintaining strong product discipline, governance, and delivery rigor. Primary Responsibilities: Design, configure, and improve business process workflows using Appian Designer, with a focus on speed to value, user-centric design, reuse of shared platform capabilities and patterns, governance, and operational control. Partner closely with business product owners, operations leaders, technology teams, and risk partners to gather requirements, map processes, define user needs, and prioritize workflow improvements. Own and manage product backlog items, including authoring, refining, and grooming user stories, acceptance criteria, specifications, process flows, UI concepts, test scenarios, and release-ready requirements. Lead stakeholder working sessions to define current-state and future-state workflows, identify friction points, iterate on MVP designs, resolve issues, and drive alignment across business and technology teams. Evaluate business requirements to identify opportunities for reuse across workflows and business areas, and partner with platform and technology teams to determine when an existing capability should be reused or extended before creating a new solution. Use AI-assisted and agentic AI tools to accelerate discovery, process analysis, requirements documentation, story drafting, workflow prototyping, test case generation, defect analysis, and delivery communications. Focus on outcomes over outputs, incorporating design thinking, analytics, business process engineering, and user feedback to inform product decisions and continuous improvement. Support QA, UAT, regression testing, and production validation by defining test scenarios, validating builds, documenting defects, gathering issue resolution requirements, and confirming readiness for release. Partner with technology teams on integration points, data dependencies, security considerations, platform constraints, and production support needs. Keep current with Appian capabilities, including Appian AI, Case Management Studio, RPA, data fabric, reporting, and platform governance, and recommend opportunities to apply new capabilities responsibly. Champion a platform-first approach and Appian best practices around governance, reusability, modular design, shared patterns, versioning, packaging, maintainability, and controlled delivery in a regulated environment. Participate in agile ceremonies, including daily standups, planning sessions, backlog refinement, demos, and retrospectives. Build and maintain Appian reports and dashboards to track workflow performance, user activity, operational quality, and business metrics; partner with senior stakeholders to define meaningful KPIs. Understand and adhere to the Company’s risk and regulatory standards, policies and controls in accordance with the Company’s Risk Appetite. Identify risk-related issues needing escalation to management. Promote an environment that supports belonging and reflects the M&T Bank brand. Maintain M&T internal control standards, including timely implementation of internal and external audit points together with any issues raised by external regulators as applicable. Complete other related duties as assigned. Education and Experience Required: Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 10 years’ business, analytical, technical, digital product, transformation, or product ownership experience, or in lieu of a degree, a combined minimum of 14 years’ higher education and/or relevant work experience, including a minimum of 10 years’ business, analytical, technical, digital product, transformation, or product ownership experience. Hands-on experience with Appian, including experience building, configuring, testing, or supporting workflows, forms, interfaces, records, process models, reports, dashboards, or related Appian objects. Experience in financial services and/or fintech, including exposure to regulated business processes, operational risk, client service, banking, wealth management, trust services, payments, capital markets, lending, compliance, or similar domains. Experience operating as a product owner, product analyst, business analyst, transformation lead, or workflow designer in an agile or iterative delivery environment. Experience writing detailed, actionable user stories, acceptance criteria, specifications, process flows, business rules, UI concepts, testing scenarios, or release documentation. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to structure ambiguous problems, assess operational impacts, analyze data or process evidence, and recommend practical solutions. Exposure to QA, UAT, regression testing, defect triage, test case development, production validation, or other solution quality practices. Working knowledge of AI-assisted tools or agentic AI concepts and the ability to use AI responsibly to improve analysis, documentation, testing, prototyping, or workflow delivery. Ability to bridge business and technical teams, translating needs into executable solutions and explaining technical constraints, risks, dependencies, and tradeoffs to stakeholders. Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to facilitate working sessions, present recommendations, document decisions, and drive alignment across teams. Ability to manage competing priorities, work independently, and deliver in a fast-paced, regulated transformation environment. Education and Experience Preferred: Appian Level 1 or higher certification, or equivalent hands-on experience with Appian Designer. Familiarity with SAIL expressions for configuring dynamic forms, validations, conditional logic, and reusable interface patterns. Understanding of Appian object reusability, versioning, packaging, release management, performance considerations, and platform governance best practices. Experience with Appian AI, Case Management Studio, Appian RPA, data fabric, connected systems, integrations, or document management workflows. Experience delivering business-specific workflows on a shared platform and identifying opportunities to reuse or extend common capabilities across multiple use cases. Experience using agentic AI or AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Open Claw, Hermes, or similar tools to support product analysis, prototyping, testing, documentation, or automation. Experience with low-code or no-code workflow platforms beyond Appian, such as Power Platform, ServiceNow, Salesforce, Pega, Airtable, Retool, Mendix, or similar tools. Strong understanding of business process mapping, process engineering, service design, user journey design, and operational improvement methods. Experience developing, managing, or launching digital capabilities in financial services, fintech, trust services, institutional services, compliance, legal operations, or document-intensive environments. Experience working in partnership with user experience, design, data, architecture, cybersecurity, risk, legal, compliance, or operations teams. Knowledge of Agile, Lean, design thinking, systems thinking, and continuous improvement principles and practices. M&T Bank is committed to fair, competitive, and market-informed pay for our employees. The pay range for this position is $148,300.00 - $247,100.00 Annual (USD). The successful candidate’s particular combination of knowledge, skills, and experience will inform their specific compensation. The range listed above corresponds to our national pay range for this role. The specific pay range applicable to you may vary based on your location. jd_text: Overview: M&T Bank is seeking a strategic and execution-oriented Escrow & Virtual Account Management (VAM) Product Manager to lead the growth, modernization, and commercialization of our escrow and virtual account solutions. The successful candidate will combine deep product management expertise with strong commercial banking knowledge to deliver differentiated solutions for clients requiring fund segregation, reconciliation, liquidity optimization, and operational efficiency. This position serves as the central point of accountability across Product, Technology, Operations, Risk, Legal, Treasury Management, and Sales teams to successfully design, launch, and enhance escrow and virtual account solutions. Primary Responsibilities: Product Strategy & Market Leadership: Develop and execute the strategic roadmap for Escrow and Virtual Account Management solutions. Identify emerging client needs, industry trends, competitive threats, and fintech opportunities. Define product positioning and value propositions across Commercial Banking, Business Banking, and specialized vertical markets. Establish multi-year product vision aligned with M&T's deposits, liquidity, and treasury management strategies. New Capability Development: Build business cases, secure funding, establish success metrics, and manage prioritization. Partner with Technology and Agile delivery teams to execute product initiatives. Drive capabilities such as: Self-service virtual account administration Virtual account-to-physical account reconciliation Enhanced reporting and analytics Treasury workstation and ERP integrations API connectivity Automated funding and sweeps Real-time payments and liquidity functionality These initiatives align with existing roadmap priorities including reconciliation tools, Treasury Center integration, balance reporting, Direct Connect integration, and enhanced escrow reporting. ​ Market Segmentation & Client Differentiation: Design product strategies tailored to the unique needs of distinct customer segments, including: Commercial Real Estate Property Management Attorney Trust Accounts Municipal Escrow 1031 Exchange Intermediaries Funeral Escrow Providers Leasing & Security Deposit Providers Large Corporate Treasury Organizations Franchise and Multi-Entity Businesses The Product Manager will be responsible for understanding the operational workflows, regulatory requirements, reconciliation challenges, and reporting needs unique to each segment and ensuring solutions are designed accordingly. M&T's escrow offering currently supports multiple specialized escrow structures across these client types. Virtual Account Management Solution Design: Lead the evolution of M&T's Virtual Account Management platform. Responsibilities include: Designing virtual account hierarchies and account structures. Defining cash concentration and fund segregation models. Supporting treasury visibility and liquidity optimization. Developing reporting and reconciliation frameworks. Building client-controlled virtual account administration capabilities. Enhancing integration with Treasury Center, APIs, ERP platforms, and treasury workstations. Supporting real-time information delivery and account governance. Commercialization & Revenue Growth: Partner with Treasury Management, Sales, Segment Management, and Marketing teams to drive product adoption. OR in lieu of a degree, A combined minimum of 11 years’ higher education and/or work experience, including a minimum of 7 years Proven product management experience in commercial banking, treasury management, liquidity solutions, or payments. title: Concrete Project Manager - Traveler
jd_text: Job Description At DPR, roles and responsibilities are more than describing a job title—they are a commitment to building great things together. The job description(s) below defines core responsibilities and the scope of the role and is a starting point. Every employee is expected to lead from where they are, take ownership of outcomes, and always act in the best interest of the team, customer, project and organization. As a purpose-driven organization on a journey to be most admired, we rely on trust, shared leadership, open communication, disciplined action and a deep respect for the individual to drive exceptional performance. Success is not just about what we build, but who we build and how we build it: with integrity, enjoyment, uniqueness and an ever-forward mindset. Job Summary: Manages Self-Perform Work (SPW) construction project individuals to deliver high-quality results and foster professional growth. Oversees the successful delivery of SPW construction projects by providing advanced expertise in self-perform construction activities, to ensure successful project execution in alignment with standards and methodologies. Manages and aligns SPW workers, subcontractors, and external partners to ensure project requirements, schedules, and quality standards are consistently achieved. Ensures efficient project execution by actively managing SPW team productivity, monitoring progress, analyzing project performance, identifying and resolving both routine and complex issues, and managing project budgets, forecasts, contracts, and cost controls to achieve financial targets and mitigate risks. Cultivates a collaborative and inclusive team environment by modeling positive leadership behaviors, fostering open communication, and actively promoting organizational values and frameworks to enhance team engagement, professional growth, and project success. Key Responsibilities: Leads, manages, and develops a team of construction SPW project individuals to achieve exceptional performance and encourage talent development. Oversees end-to-end execution of self-perform work scopes by collaborating with SPW project teams, monitoring progress, and addressing escalated, complex issues to ensure timely completion. Oversees and approves procurement of SPW-specific materials, equipment, and specialty trade subcontractors as needed, ensuring timely delivery and alignment with SPW work sequences and field requirements. Communicates SPW project status, risks, and changes to stakeholders, leveraging advanced knowledge in SPW means and methods. Evaluates SPW project performance, identifies areas for improvement, and implements corrective actions. Reviews comprehensive SPW project documentation for compliance, reporting, and future reference, while actively managing project costs and forecasting to support financial control and informed decision-making. Education Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in construction management, engineering, architecture, a related field, or equivalent experience required. Work Experience: 7 years of experience in construction engineering, project engineering, or a related field required. 1 - 2 years of experience in a managerial capacity preferred. Certifications and Licenses: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) 30-Hour Construction certification preferred. OSHA 30 program completion within 6 months of hire is required. DPR Construction is a forward-thinking, self-performing general contractor specializing in technically complex and sustainable projects for the advanced technology, life sciences, healthcare, higher education and commercial markets. Founded in 1990, DPR is a great story of entrepreneurial success as a private, employee-owned company that has grown into a multi-billion-dollar family of companies with offices around the world. Working at DPR, you'll have the chance to try new things, explore paths and shape your future. Here, we build opportunity together—by harnessing our talents, enabling curiosity and pursuing our collective ambition to make the best ideas happen. We are proud to be recognized as a great place to work by our talented teammates and leading news organizations like U.S. News and World Report, Forbes, Fast Company and Newsweek. Explore our open opportunities at www.dpr.com/careers .

title: Senior Product Manager
jd_text: Senior Product Manager North Hospitality - Remote Join the hospitality experts. Imagine delivering sophisticated hospitality technology, simplified payment processing, and award-winning support to some of the top restaurants in the U.S. North is seeking a highly detail-oriented and technically proficient Senior Product Manager to drive the execution of our product roadmap and oversee the delivery of innovative, high-impact solutions in the payments and fintech space. You will serve as the technical backbone of the product team, collaborating closely with multiple Agile engineering teams to translate strategic vision into actionable, detailed requirements and deliverables. Daily decisions include prioritization, value, timelines, risk management, and functionality for the Developer Experience Team’s product. The Product Manager is able to understand not only the business needs and value, but has an understanding of the technical and system aspects impacted by the projects and business needs. As the Senior Product Manager, you will dig deep into technical details, coordinate complex cross-functional initiatives, and ensure that our products meet the highest standards of quality, reliability, and customer value. You will be responsible for managing and optimizing workflows using Jira and other product management tools, and will play a key role in aligning internal and external stakeholders. This role is ideal for someone who thrives on technical complexity, is relentless about details, can drive order out from multiple competing priorities, and is passionate about building products for developers in FinTech. What you'll do: Technical Product Ownership: Own the end-to-end product lifecycle for assigned product areas, from ideation through delivery and ongoing optimization, with a strong emphasis on technical requirements and system integrations. Deep Technical Engagement: Work closely with Agile engineering teams (internal and external) to break down complex business needs into detailed technical requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria. Agile Leadership: Act as Product Owner for one or more products, providing clear vision, direction, and detailed requirements. Lead backlog grooming, sprint planning, and prioritization using Jira. Stakeholder Coordination: Gather and synthesize input from internal teams (engineering, product, leadership, sales, and support) and external partners/customers. Ensure alignment and transparency around product decisions, progress, and trade-offs. Data-Driven Decision Making: Develop and own processes and tools to collect, analyze, and present data that informs prioritization, risk management, and release planning. Release & Roadmap Management: Own and maintain a detailed product roadmap and backlog. Ensure visibility and communication of progress, risks, and changes to all stakeholders. Quality & Compliance: Ensure all deliverables meet North’s Definition of Ready and Definition of Done. Proactively manage escalations and communicate impact of expedited or unplanned work. Continuous Improvement: Collaborate with other Product Managers and leadership to refine and improve product management best practices across North. What we need from you: Bachelor’s (BA or BS) or equivalent experience. Four years previous experience as a Product Manager, Product Engineer, Product Analyst, or similar technical product roles. Proven experience working with Agile software development teams. Strong proficiency with Jira and modern product management software. Product Owner Certification (CSPO, etc.) preferred. Payments or fintech industry experience highly preferred. Exceptional attention to detail and technical depth; able to dive into system architecture, APIs, and data flows. Advanced knowledge of Agile methodologies and best practices; experience as a Product Owner on Scrum teams. Demonstrated ability to break down complex business and technical problems into actionable requirements and deliverables. Skilled in backlog management, roadmap planning, and cross-team coordination. Strong analytical skills; able to leverage data to drive prioritization and decision-making. Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to convey technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Customer-focused mindset with a passion for delivering high-value products. Proactive, self-motivated, and able to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. Innovative thinker who embraces change and continuous improvement. Travel Requirements: Up to 20% License and Certification Requirements: CSPO or similar Agile certification preferred What we offer: We offer a comprehensive benefits package that enables our teams to live a life well lived, both personally and professionally. Some of our perks include: Medical, Dental, & Vision Coverage Flexible Paid Time Off 401(k) + Match Education Assistance Paid Maternity & Paternity Leave Mental Health Support & Well-Being Program Company-funded Lifestyle Spending Account Salary Range: $115,000 to $135,000 Pay within this range varies by work location and on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. We look forward to discussing your salary expectations and our full total rewards offerings throughout the interview process. Who we are: We are restaurateurs building products for restaurateurs. At North Hospitality, our team has years of experience working in, and for, some of the most renowned hotels and restaurants in the country. Now, we’re committed to bringing that passion to restaurateurs everywhere in the form of a single, seamless platform for all operations. At North, we celebrate diversity and create an inclusive environment for everyone. We are an equal-opportunity employer. To learn more about North and our family of companies, visit our website: https://www.north.com/company/about/our-companies-brands

Combining a flexible, intelligent platform with end-to-end payments capabilities and services developed through its deep industry experience, NCR Voyix empowers retailers and restaurants to accelerate new possibilities for their operations, experiences and business outcomes. NCR Voyix is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, and serves customers in more than 35 countries worldwide. Department: Payments Hardware & Deployment Reports To: Director / Executive Director, Deployment Position Type: Full-Time Location: Irving, TX Position Summary The Product Manager, Payments Hardware & Deployment is responsible for supporting the lifecycle, certification, release, and operational readiness of payment hardware solutions. This role serves as a key connection point between Product, Deployment, Technology, Operations, Sales, Finance, vendors, suppliers, logistics partners, and other internal stakeholders to ensure payment devices are successfully evaluated, certified, launched, deployed, supported, and managed throughout their lifecycle. The Product Manager will manage a portfolio of payment hardware products while supporting the operational processes required to deliver those products to customers. The role requires a combination of product management, payments industry knowledge, project coordination, vendor management, and operational execution. This individual will help drive product readiness, improve deployment execution, strengthen vendor and supplier relationships, reduce operational risk, and ensure the organization can efficiently scale its payments hardware capabilities as business needs evolve. Key Responsibilities Product & Hardware Lifecycle Management Manage payment hardware products throughout the product lifecycle, from evaluation and onboarding through deployment, maintenance, and end-of-life. Coordinate new payment device evaluations and provide recommendations based on business requirements, customer needs, functionality, cost, and operational considerations. Develop and maintain product requirements in partnership with business, technology, operations, and deployment stakeholders. Support product roadmap planning and prioritization for payment hardware initiatives. Monitor product performance, industry trends, market developments, and competitive offerings to identify opportunities for improvement. Coordinate end-of-life and replacement strategies for hardware products to minimize customer and operational disruption. Maintain accurate documentation related to supported devices, configurations, capabilities, dependencies, and lifecycle status. Product Releases & Certifications Manage payment hardware release activities from initial planning through production readiness. Coordinate hardware and solution certification activities with internal teams, payment processors, manufacturers, vendors, and other applicable partners. Track certification requirements, dependencies, testing activities, defects, and outstanding deliverables. Ensure appropriate stakeholders are aligned on release scope, timelines, risks, and readiness criteria. Identify and escalate risks that could impact certification, release, deployment, or customer commitments. Partner with technical and operational teams to ensure new products are operationally ready before deployment. Coordinate post-release activities and capture lessons learned to continuously improve future product launches. Deployment & Operational Readiness Partner closely with Deployment teams to ensure payments products can be successfully ordered, configured, provisioned, injected, fulfilled, shipped, installed, and supported. Define and document operational requirements associated with new payment hardware and product launches. Support the development and improvement of deployment workflows, procedures, controls, and documentation. Coordinate cross-functional activities required to move products from certification into operational deployment. Identify process gaps and opportunities to improve deployment efficiency, quality, scalability, and the customer experience. Support resolution of product-related issues affecting deployments or customers. Assist with deployment initiatives and projects requiring Product Management ownership or coordination. Vendor, Supplier & Partner Management Develop and maintain strong relationships with payments hardware manufacturers, suppliers, logistics providers, and other external partners. Coordinate vendor deliverables, product roadmaps, hardware availability, lead times, certifications, and product changes. Monitor vendor performance and escalate issues that could impact business operations or customer commitments. Partner with internal Procurement and Finance teams as needed to support hardware purchasing, forecasting, and vendor-related activities. Coordinate across the supply chain to identify and resolve hardware availability, fulfillment, logistics, or operational issues. Serve as a primary point of contact for designated product and vendor relationships. Cross-Functional Leadership Serve as a central point of coordination across Product, Technology, Deployment, Operations, Finance, Sales, Support, Compliance, and other stakeholders. Translate business and customer needs into clear product and operational requirements. Facilitate working sessions to drive decisions, resolve dependencies, and maintain alignment across stakeholders. Communicate product status, risks, dependencies, and key decisions to leadership and business partners. Coordinate multiple initiatives simultaneously while managing competing priorities and deadlines. Promote accountability by clearly defining owners, deliverables, timelines, and escalation paths. Process Improvement & Documentation Develop and maintain product documentation, procedures, requirements, workflows, and operational reference materials. Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce manual effort, improve controls, and minimize operational errors. Establish repeatable processes that support business continuity and organizational scalability. Develop appropriate tracking and reporting for product releases, certifications, vendor activities, and deployment readiness. Capture institutional knowledge to reduce dependency on individual resources and strengthen business continuity. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Business, Product Management, Technology, Finance, Operations, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience. 3+ years of experience in Product Management, Product Operations, Payments, FinTech, Operations, Deployment, or a related field. Experience managing products, projects, or operational initiatives involving multiple stakeholders. Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced environment. Strong project coordination and organizational skills. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Experience working with external vendors, suppliers, or business partners. Ability to identify operational risks, dependencies, and process improvement opportunities. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities. Preferred Qualifications Experience within the payments, merchant acquiring, financial technology, or payment processing industry. Knowledge of point-of-sale terminals and payment hardware. Experience with payment device certification and release processes. Familiarity with payment terminal manufacturers and hardware suppliers. Understanding of PCI-related requirements and payment security concepts. Familiarity with payment terminal configuration, encryption, key injection, or Key Injection Facility operations. Experience working with logistics, fulfillment, inventory, or hardware deployment organizations. Experience managing hardware lifecycle and end-of-life initiatives. Key Competencies The successful candidate will demonstrate: Ownership: Takes accountability for initiatives from planning through execution. Execution: Can effectively move initiatives through complex cross-functional environments. Collaboration: Builds strong relationships across technical, operational, commercial, and external teams. Risk Management: Identifies issues and dependencies before they negatively affect customers or delivery. Customer Focus: Understands how product and operational decisions ultimately affect merchants and customers. Continuous Improvement: Looks for opportunities to simplify processes and improve quality and efficiency. Adaptability: Effectively manages changing priorities and evolving business requirements. Communication: Clearly communicates status, risks, decisions, and expectations across all levels of the organization. Experience managing long, complex sales cycles involving multiple customer and internal stakeholders. Ability to establish credibility with senior executives, operational leaders, technology stakeholders, procurement teams, and other decision-makers. Strong commercial judgment, negotiation capability, and financial acumen. Experience developing account strategies, opportunity plans, business cases, and executive presentations. Ability to communicate the value of a portfolio that may include hardware, software, services, subscriptions, and recurring-revenue solutions. Strong pipeline-management and forecasting discipline. Willingness and ability to travel extensively throughout North America, frequently and with limited notice when required. Ability to operate independently in a field-based environment while remaining closely connected to a cross-functional organization. Valid driver’s license and ability to satisfy applicable customer-site and gaming-licensing requirements. Experience selling technology platforms or solutions that are integrated into mission-critical customer operations. Track record of competitive displacement, greenfield sales, or significant product penetration. Familiarity with casino operations, player loyalty, bonusing, analytics, casino accounting, customer engagement, or systems integration. Experience selling a combination of capital products and recurring software or services. Understanding of SaaS, cloud-based delivery, subscription offerings, or technology modernization. Experience working effectively across product, engineering, services, finance, contracts, and executive leadership teams. title: Enterprise Services Architect
jd_text: At Mitel, you will have the opportunity to help businesses connect, collaborate and provide better experiences for our customers. You will deliver valuable contributions in creating business success within our global organization utilizing your unique attributes, skills and experience. Please take a moment to look over this opportunity and if interested, feel free to send us your application. About the Role We are seeking a strategic and technically astute Enterprise Services Architect to lead the design of Professional Services and Managed Services solutions for large enterprise customers, including net new customer acquisitions. This role bridges the gap between sales, delivery, and operations — translating complex customer needs into scalable, repeatable, and profitable service offerings. You will engage directly with enterprise customers to architect end-to-end services solutions that accelerate deployment, enhance adoption, and deliver long-term value.
